## Summary

Containerises the web shell (already on main from PR #2) and adds the Fly app config so Milestone 1 in [docs/ops.md](../blob/main/docs/ops.md#1-milestone-1--hello-kno) reaches a live URL.

Currently in **Shaping**. TDD cycles begin when flipped to In Progress.

## TDD approach (no self-granted exemptions this time)

Previous attempt (closed PR #4) claimed a "config files are TDD-exempt" exemption that AGENTS.md doesn't grant. This time every behavior has a test:

1. \`fly.toml\` parse + shape — pytest reads TOML, asserts `internal_port=8080`, health check `path=/api/health`, mount config. Red → write fly.toml → Green.
2. Container builds — real `docker build`. Red (no Dockerfile) → write Dockerfile → Green.
3. Container responds — `docker run` on ephemeral port + curl. Red → tune CMD → Green.

Slow tests are gated behind a new `poe test-docker` task so the inner loop stays fast.

## Summary

An always-on AI Marketing Manager surface for **CRBRL.AI**, built as a self-contained React app with five integrated pillars:

- **Listening** — 3× daily scans (Morning / Midday / Evening UTC) across X, Reddit, Discord, Telegram, Farcaster, LinkedIn, YouTube, Hacker News, and TikTok. Each scan ships a written agent summary, sentiment mix, theme ranking, source breakdown, and a live post stream with per-post sentiment scores.
- **Ideation** — campaign concepts auto-derived from the day's dominant themes, each with a stance (offensive / defensive / balanced), platform mix, hook, CTA, estimated reach, and confidence score.
- **Content Studio** — three still variants and a 45-second video storyboard per campaign, with per-platform aspect ratios for IG, X, LinkedIn, and YouTube.
- **Scheduler** — 7-day, multi-platform queue placed at empirically-optimal UTC slots per platform (Sprout / Hootsuite / Buffer 2024 averages, baked into the engine).
- **A/B Lab** — live experiments with 2-proportion z-test significance, lift %, automatic promote/revert decisions, and a 30-day learning curve across CTR / engagement / conversion.

The engine (`src/marketing/agentEngine.js`) is deterministic and seedable so the UI is reproducible. It's designed to be a drop-in shell over real services later: X v2, Reddit, IG/LinkedIn/YouTube Graph APIs for listening; Claude / GPT for ideation; Flux / Sora / Veo for creative; Buffer or native Graph APIs for scheduling; and an in-house contextual bandit for experimentation.

## What's in the diff

- `src/marketing/agentEngine.js` — listening, ideation, asset gen, scheduling, A/B, and learning-curve generators (with a `runFullCycle()` orchestrator)
- `src/marketing/CRBRLMarketingManager.jsx` — full dashboard UI with animated panels, recharts visualizations, and per-platform creative previews

author: ostheimer
body:
## Summary
Closes the last Weglot-feature gap on the switcher side: site owners can override the canonical flag per language for regional audiences:
- `en` → 🇺🇸 (US) instead of 🇬🇧 (GB)
- `pt` → 🇧🇷 (BR) instead of 🇵🇹 (PT)
- `es` → 🇲🇽 (MX) instead of 🇪🇸 (ES)
- etc.

### New option
`switcher_custom_flags` assoc array `<lang, emoji|url>`. Empty by default — existing sites keep their canonical flags untouched.

### Renderer
Emits a scoped `<style class="deepglot-switcher__custom-flags">` block before `<aside>`:
- **Emoji value** → `.deepglot-flag--{lang}::before { content: "🇺🇸" }`
- **URL value** → `.deepglot-flag--{lang} { background-image: url(…) } + ::before { content: "" }` (reset so default emoji doesn't stack)

### Sanitisation
- Drop keys that aren't valid ISO codes or not in source ∪ targets (stale rows stop injecting CSS)
- Drop empty values
- Strip CSS string break-out chars (`" ' ; { } < > \`) so hostile pastes can't escape the content/url() context
- Cap value length at 256 chars so a 5 KB paste can't bloat the `<head>`

### Admin UI
Sprachumschalter section gets a per-language text input table — one row per configured language with placeholder examples for both emoji and URL formats.

## Test plan
- [x] `SwitcherCustomFlagsTest.php` (10 blocks): defaults, configured-language filtering, XSS char stripping, length cap, accessor, no-overrides clean output, emoji + URL render variants, emit-order (`<style>` before `<aside>`), runtime-config sub-object.
- [x] All 21 PHP tests green.
- [ ] After deploy: visual test on meinhaushalt.at — override `en` → 🇺🇸 and confirm the flag changes in the switcher.

author: chanyavrc
body:
## Summary

Two compounding optimizer bugs caused `A if cond else B` inside a function body to fail when `cond` was a local and the result was consumed:

- **`pass_dead_store_elim`** walked instructions linearly and treated the `then`-arm's write to the merge temp as dead because the `else`-arm wrote the same temp shortly after — ignoring the unconditional jump that separates them.  Eliminating the then-arm's `LoadConst` left the temp unset on the taken path, raising `internal: temp register read before write`.
- **`pass_const_fold`** cleared its known-constant map only at backward jump targets (loop headers), not at general merge points.  After the temp-register crash was fixed this exposed a second bug: `("OK" if c else "FAIL") + "!"` folded to `"FAIL!"` regardless of `c`.

Both passes are now control-flow aware: DSE conservatively keeps a store if any control-flow instruction precedes the next apparent write, and const-fold clears the known map at every basic-block boundary.

## Test plan

- [x] Repro `def f(c): x = 1 if c else 2; print(x)` — prints `1` / `2` (matched against CPython).
- [x] All "what also fails" cases from the issue body run with CPython parity (assigned-then-concat, nested ternary, ternary in `print` call).
- [x] All "what works (for contrast)" cases still work (module-scope ternary, literal-condition, direct-return, if/else statement form).
- [x] Added optimizer unit tests: `dse_keeps_then_branch_write_across_jump`, `const_fold_clears_at_forward_jump_target`.
- [x] Added parity fixture: `crates/pyrust/tests/cases/language/test_cond_expr_in_function.py`.
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` clean.
- [x] `cargo test --release --bin pyrust` — 274 passed.
- [x] `cargo test --release --test parity_compare` — passed.
- [x] `cargo test -p pyrust-derive --test trybuild` — passed.

Closes #361.

author: jkheadley
body:
## Summary

Ships F-7 from `docs/specs/SELF-HEALING-REMEDIATOR-V2-SPEC.md` (§R1 Upgrade invariants + §A35 backup/sync wiring + §A50 hook-shape corrections + §A57 Tier-2). Two new primitives plus the A35 const-literal hook-shape changes.

- **`MigratorStepEngine`** (new module `src/core/MigratorStepEngine.ts`) — register named, idempotent atomic steps with a semver `version: string`. `runPendingSteps(from, to)` executes pending steps once per version. Ledger at `<stateDir>/migrator-steps-completed.json` keyed by `<version>:<step-name>`. Failed steps record `outcome: 'failed'` and do NOT roll back prior steps or block subsequent steps.
- **`AnnouncementManager`** (same module) — `announceOnce(id, message, channel)` primitive for "show this once, never again". Ledger at `<stateDir>/announcements-shown.json`. Ledger is recorded BEFORE the sink fires so a flaky sink cannot cause duplicate emission.
- **Additive on `PostUpdateMigrator`** — new `registerStep` + async `runPendingSteps` methods backed by a lazy engine. The existing `MigratorConfig` constructor + all 15 existing `migrate*` methods + `migrate()` orchestrator are unchanged.
- **A35 hook-shape** — `GitStateManager.DEFAULT_GITIGNORE` const literal carries the five remediation runtime path globs; exported as `REMEDIATION_GITIGNORE_ENTRIES`. `BackupManager` gains `REMEDIATION_EXCLUDED_PATH_PREFIXES` const + optional 5th constructor arg `isRemediationEnabled` that parallels `isIntegratedBeingEnabled`. Gate ON drops user-added remediation-prefixed `includeFiles`; OFF/absent preserves back-compat for every existing caller. No new plugin/register API per §A50.

No production wiring yet. Tier-2 surfaces (W-2..W-4, S-1..S-3) will register their own steps via `migrator.registerStep(...)` and surface migration outcomes via `announcer.announceOnce(...)`.

Side-effects review: `upgrades/side-effects/f7-post-update-migrator-atomic-step.md`.

## Test plan

- [x] 8 new tests in `tests/unit/PostUpdateMigrator-atomicStep.test.ts` — step runs once + records, subsequent runs skip, failed step doesn't block others, future-version skipped without ledger entry, state persists across instances, semver compare correctness.
- [x] 5 new tests in `tests/unit/AnnouncementManager.test.ts` — first-true/subsequent-false, independent ids, persistence, sink-throw cannot cause re-emission, input validation.
- [x] 5 new tests in `tests/unit/PostUpdateMigrator-a35-remediationPaths.test.ts` — `DEFAULT_GITIGNORE` contains all five entries, `REMEDIATION_EXCLUDED_PATH_PREFIXES` exported, gate ON drops, gate OFF preserves, absent callback = back-compat.
- [x] All 76 pre-existing `PostUpdateMigrator-*` tests pass unchanged.
- [x] All 47 `BackupManager*` + `git-state-manager` tests pass unchanged.
- [x] Full suite: 83 files / 2437 tests pass; `tsc --noEmit` clean.

author: abhidevepl
body:
🚨 **Severity:** CRITICAL

💡 **Vulnerability:** The `googleAuth` controller was insecurely trusting the `email` and `name` fields provided in the request body from the client. This "Trust-on-First-Use" (TOFU) pattern allowed for trivial authentication bypass and account impersonation.

🎯 **Impact:** An attacker could gain unauthorized access to any user account by simply knowing their email address and making a direct API call to `/api/auth/google`, potentially leading to full account takeover and data exposure.

🔧 **Fix Summary:**
1.  **Backend Verification:** Integrated the `firebase-admin` SDK to verify the Firebase ID token sent by the client. The server now extracts the user's identity (email, name) only from the cryptographically verified token.
2.  **Frontend Update:** Modified the frontend authentication flow to retrieve the ID token after a successful Google sign-in and securely transmit it to the backend.
3.  **Testing & Documentation:** Added Jest unit tests to verify the new secure authentication logic and provided an `.env.example` file to document the required Firebase credentials.

✅ **Verification:**
-   Performed syntax validation on all new and modified backend files using `node --check`.
-   Executed the new unit test suite in the `server` directory (`npm test`), confirming that all 4 security-related test cases pass.
-   Verified frontend code consistency and linting using `npm run lint`.
-   Updated `.jules/sentinel.md` with critical learnings from this vulnerability.

author: franksong2702
body:
Refs #2215 (Fix B).

## Thinking Path
Issue #2215 identified a pre-existing `re.MULTILINE` hazard in the "the user is asking" strip pattern. Removing `MULTILINE` alone prevents mid-response stripping, but it also stops stripping a leading wrapper line when a real answer follows on the next line. The correct narrow fix is to strip only the leading wrapper line.

## What Changed
- Updated `api/streaming.py::_strip_thinking_markup()` so the "the user is asking" cleanup consumes only the leading wrapper line:

```python
r"^\s*(the|ther)\s+user\s+is\s+asking[^\n]*(?:\n|$)"
```

- Added regression coverage proving a leading wrapper line is removed while the visible answer remains.
- Added regression coverage proving a mid-response "The user is asking..." line is preserved as normal prose.

## Why It Matters
This keeps the intended title-wrapper cleanup without deleting legitimate mid-response content. It also avoids regressing multi-line leading wrapper cases where the wrapper line should disappear but the answer should remain.

## Verification
- `pytest -q tests/test_issue607.py tests/test_issues_853_857.py tests/test_sprint38.py`
- `python -m py_compile api/streaming.py tests/test_issue607.py`
- `git diff --check`

## Risks / Follow-ups
- This is a focused regex cleanup and does not change the broader reasoning-wrapper handling from #2213.
- This is only Fix B from #2215; Fix A is tracked separately in #2216, so this PR intentionally uses `Refs` rather than auto-closing #2215.

body:
## Summary

Closes #374. Pre-fix, the confirmation modal shown when a user clicks Approve only carried a static sentence and the execution UUID — not informed consent for a financial commitment.

This PR introduces a new `frontend/src/approval-details.ts` module that builds a rich modal body:

- **Aggregate header** — total upfront, total monthly + annual savings, commitment count, distinct providers, distinct accounts touched.
- **Per-rec table** (12 columns) — account (Name + external ID), provider, service, resource type, engine, region, count, term, payment, upfront, monthly savings, effective savings %.

## Per-rec field sources

| Column | Source |
|---|---|
| Account | `/api/accounts` lookup keyed off `rec.cloud_account_id` → `Name (external_id)` |
| Provider / Service / Resource / Region | direct from `rec` |
| Engine | `rec.engine`, present on RDS / Aurora / OpenSearch / ElastiCache; "—" otherwise |
| Term / Payment | direct from `rec` via existing `formatTerm` |
| Upfront / Monthly savings | direct from `rec` via existing `formatCurrency` |
| Effective savings % | `rec.savings / rec.on_demand_cost` when baseline present, falls back to `savings / (monthly + savings)` reconstruction, "—" when neither is usable |

The external-ID column does triple duty: AWS account number, Azure subscription ID, GCP project — all flow through the existing `CloudAccount.external_id` field. Recs without an account (ambient-credentials direct-execute path) render as `(ambient)`.

## Call sites wired

- `frontend/src/history.ts` — dashboard Approve button on pending rows.
- `frontend/src/purchases-deeplink.ts` — email-link approve flow.

The Cancel-purchase deep link keeps the legacy text body — cancelling a pending approval doesn't commit cloud spend, so the cost-of-error asymmetry doesn't justify the extra fetch.

## Resilience

`buildApprovalDetailsBody(executionId)` fetches details + accounts list in parallel and falls back to the legacy sentence if either GET fails. The Approve button keeps working on stale caches, 403s, or transient network failures — just without the details.

## CSS

`components.css` widens `.modal-confirm` to `min(1100px, 95vw)` only when it contains an `.approval-details` element (via `:has()`), so the other confirmDialog callers (Cancel, Delete, etc.) keep their 480px layout. The 12-col table is sticky-header + horizontally scrollable for narrow viewports, capped at 50vh.

## Tests

`frontend/src/__tests__/approval-details.test.ts` — 20 unit tests on `renderApprovalDetailsBody` + the pure helpers. Covers:

- Header aggregates (totals, distinct providers, distinct accounts)
- Full 12-column table headers
- Account UUID resolution: known → `Name (external_id)`, unknown → `acct <prefix>…`, missing → `(ambient)`
- Engine column for RDS-shaped recs, "—" otherwise
- Term and currency formatting matches existing dashboard conventions
- Effective savings % with baseline vs. reconstruction vs. neither
- Multi-provider / multi-account aggregate counts
- Empty-recs fallback
- HTML escaping of user-controlled string values
- `formatAccountLabel` and `computeEffectiveSavingsPct` edge cases (zero baseline, missing fields)

## Test plan

- [x] `npx jest` — 1666 tests pass (47 suites)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [ ] Manual: open the Approve modal on a pending row in dev, confirm: per-rec table renders, account name + external ID resolved, engine column shows for RDS / blank for EC2, effective savings % shows when baseline present.

## Backend changes

None. The backend's `buildPurchaseDetailsResponse` already returns the full `recommendations[]` array and `total_upfront_cost` / `estimated_savings`. Only the TypeScript `PurchaseDetails` type was stale — it has been brought into sync with the actual response shape.

## Summary
Adds `.github/workflows/mirror-to-synthminds.yml` — a `workflow_dispatch` Action that runs `git clone --mirror` + `git push --mirror` on a GitHub-hosted runner, allowing the entire `SynthmindsLLC/SynthBrain` repo to be mirrored to `Synthminds/SynthBrain` from anywhere with a web browser (including mobile).

## Why
The CLI mirror runbook requires a terminal. This Action lets the mirror be triggered from the GitHub mobile web UI (Actions → Run workflow), no shell needed.

## Setup required (one-time)
1. Create empty repo at `Synthminds/SynthBrain` on github.com.
2. Create a fine-grained PAT on the `Synthminds` account scoped to `Synthminds/SynthBrain` with **Contents: read and write**.
3. On `SynthmindsLLC/SynthBrain`: Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret → name `MIRROR_TOKEN`, value = the PAT.
4. Trigger: Actions → "Mirror to Synthminds/SynthBrain" → Run workflow.

## Inputs
- `target_repo` (default: `Synthminds/SynthBrain`) — override only if mirroring elsewhere.

## Safety
- `permissions: contents: read` on the job (least privilege).
- Validates the PAT exists and `target_repo` matches `owner/name` format before pushing.
- `concurrency` group prevents simultaneous runs.
- 15-minute timeout.

## What we found Three instances of weak encryption algorithm usage in `BenchmarkTest00615.java`: | Line | Vulnerability | Detection Rule | |------|---|---| | 67 | `Cipher.getInstance("DES/CBC/PKCS5Padding")` | Des Is Deprecated | | 70 | `KeyGenerator.getInstance("DES")` | Des Is Deprecated | | 70 | `KeyGenerator.getInstance("DES")` | DESede Is Deprecated | **CWE:** [CWE-326 Inadequate Encryption](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/326.html) **Severity:** Medium **Detected By:** OpenGrep --- ## Why this matters DES (Data Encryption Standard) uses a 56-bit effective key length that is cryptographically broken. Modern hardware can exhaust the entire DES keyspace via brute-force attack in hours. NIST formally withdrew DES in 2005 and has deprecated its use for all new applications. In this codebase: - Line 67 instantiates the cipher with the hardcoded weak algorithm `"DES/CBC/PKCS5Padding"` - Line 70 generates a 56-bit DES key via `KeyGenerator.getInstance("DES")` - The encrypted output is written to a file labeled `passwordFile.txt` with the key `secret_value=...`, indicating security-sensitive use - The servlet is publicly mapped at `/crypto-00/BenchmarkTest00615` with no authentication gates observed **Risk if not fixed:** An attacker with access to the encrypted ciphertext can recover the plaintext by exhaustively searching the 56-bit keyspace on commodity hardware, compromising the confidentiality of the encrypted secret value. --- ## Why we're changing it The fix replaces all three DES references with AES: 1. **Line 64:** IV seed size updated from `8` → `16` bytes (AES/CBC requires a 16-byte IV matching its 128-bit block size) 2. **Line 67:** Cipher algorithm updated from `"DES/CBC/PKCS5Padding"` → `"AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding"` 3. **Line 70:** KeyGenerator algorithm updated from `"DES"` → `"AES"` (generates 128-bit keys by default, NIST-approved) AES in CBC mode with PKCS5Padding is a NIST-approved, widely vetted symmetric cipher. The CBC mode and PKCS5Padding are preserved to maintain structural compatibility while eliminating the weak algorithm. **Alternatives considered:** - **AES/GCM/NoPadding:** Provides authenticated encryption (confidentiality + integrity), stronger than CBC but requires a 96-bit nonce and GCM-specific tag handling. Rejected to minimize change scope while fully addressing the CWE-326 findings. - **Triple-DES (3DES/DESede):** Already flagged as deprecated; NIST deprecated 3DES for new applications in 2019 (SP 800-131A Rev. 2). Rejected. - **Keeping DES with a longer key:** Not possible; DES key length is fixed at 56 bits by the algorithm specification and cannot be extended. --- ## How we confirmed **Automated checks:** - Static analysis via OpenGrep confirmed hardcoded DES algorithm strings at lines 67 and 70 - Codebase inspection confirmed no conditional algorithm selection or suppression annotations - File I/O analysis confirmed encrypted output is written to persistent storage with security-sensitive labeling **Manual verification:** - Reviewed servlet mapping: `@WebServlet(value = "/crypto-00/BenchmarkTest00615")` confirms public HTTP entry point - Traced encryption flow: no attacker-controlled branching between servlet entry and cipher instantiation at line 67 - Confirmed IV generation uses `SecureRandom` (line 64), but IV freshness cannot compensate for DES's 56-bit key exhaustion vulnerability ### Vulnerability Flow Diagram ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme':'base','themeVariables':{'fontFamily':'ui-sans-serif, Inter, system-ui, sans-serif','primaryColor':'#EDE9FE','primaryTextColor':'#1A1A2E','primaryBorderColor':'#7C3AED','lineColor':'#5B21B6','secondaryColor':'#FEF3C7','tertiaryColor':'#DCFCE7'}}}%% flowchart TD A["HTTP Request to

Problem
Background tabs don't update — When an agent finishes running, non-active browser tabs don't see running: false until the user clicks on them
Alpine "Duplicate key" console errors — The allItems getter can return duplicate items during the race between server poll updates and pending item cleanup

author: nkanf-dev
body:
## Problem

Shell commands run as a process tree (e.g. `bash -c "sleep 30 & sleep 30 &"`). When a timeout fires, `process.Kill()` only kills the direct child — the grandchild processes keep running as orphans.

## Fix

Use `Setpgid` to put each shell into its own process group, and `Kill(-pgid, SIGKILL)` to kill the entire group at once.

`syscall.Setpgid` and `syscall.Kill` are POSIX-only — they don't exist on Windows. That's why the platform-specific logic is split into two files with build tags:

| File | Build tag | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `shell_kill_unix.go` | `unix` | `Setpgid` + `Kill(-pgid)` |
| `shell_kill_windows.go` | `windows` | `taskkill /T /F /PID` (kills process tree) |

body:
## Summary

Phase A of the Strava integration plan ([docs/plans/2026-05-13-003-feat-strava-integration-plan.md](docs/plans/2026-05-13-003-feat-strava-integration-plan.md)). Foundational scaffolding that Phases B-D will consume.

- **A1 -- Token encryption module** ([apps/web/src/security/token-crypto.ts](apps/web/src/security/token-crypto.ts)). AES-256-GCM via `node:crypto`. Versioned keys via `STRAVA_TOKEN_KEYS=v:hex,...`; highest version for new encryptions, all listed versions retained for decryption. Layout `iv(12) || authTag(16) || ciphertext(N)`.
- **A2 -- Inngest scaffold** ([apps/web/app/api/inngest/route.ts](apps/web/app/api/inngest/route.ts), [client.ts](apps/web/src/inngest/client.ts), [functions/index.ts](apps/web/src/inngest/functions/index.ts)). Serve handler at `/api/inngest`; zero functions registered today (Phase C+D add backfill / hydration / matcher). `signingKey` wired through `serve()` and the `Inngest` client.
- **A3 -- Boot env validator** ([apps/web/src/config.ts](apps/web/src/config.ts)). Eager `config` singleton that throws at module import in production if Strava secrets are missing or contain placeholders (`'', 'xxx', 'hex', all-zeros`). Validates `STRAVA_TOKEN_KEYS` version numbers + duplicate detection so it agrees with token-crypto's parser. Warns (does not throw) on missing Inngest event/signing keys.
- **A4 -- Sport normalization map** ([apps/web/src/strava/sport-normalization.ts](apps/web/src/strava/sport-normalization.ts)). Hand-authored Strava `sport_type` -> canonical `Sport` enum. Null-prototype object so `'__proto__'` / `'constructor'` etc. cannot leak through; falls back to `'other'`.

Plus docs: [docs/solutions/strava-token-crypto.md](docs/solutions/strava-token-crypto.md), [docs/solutions/inngest-setup.md](docs/solutions/inngest-setup.md), and updated `apps/web/.env.example`. Plan checkboxes A1-A4 ticked.

## Review

`ce:review` ran 10 reviewers (always-on 6 + security, kieran-typescript, reliability, adversarial). 11 cross-reviewer findings auto-fixed in commit `d343e8c`:

| # | Issue | Reviewers | Fix |
|---|-------|-----------|-----|
| 1 | `INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY` missing from validator + not wired | correctness, project-standards, reliability, security, adversarial | Boot warning + passed to `serve()` and client |
| 2 | `config` singleton documented but not exported | correctness, reliability, kieran-typescript, agent-native | Eager `export const config = loadConfig()` |
| 3 | `__reset*ForTests` exports dead + reachable | maintainability, kieran-typescript, security, reliability, adversarial | Removed both; tests use `vi.resetModules()` |
| 4 | Inline secret-gen command (AGENTS.md "Secrets") | project-standards (2 sites) | 0600-file / shred pattern |
| 5 | Sport map prototype-chain pollution + type lie | kieran-typescript, adversarial | `Object.create(null)` + `Sport \| undefined` type |
| 6 | Config validator missed version-num + dup checks | adversarial, security, maintainability | Added `Number.isInteger >= 1` + `seenVersions` |
| 7 | Weak `.toThrow()` + vacuous `.not.toThrow()` | testing | Narrowed regex; capture+inspect actual error |
| 8 | Missing test coverage for 7 scenarios | testing, kieran-typescript, adversarial | +7 tests (now 59 total) |
| 9 | Plan/code Inngest id mismatch (`da2` vs `da2-web`) | agent-native | Plan updated |
| 10 | Defensible non-null assertion lacked comment | kieran-typescript (info) | Comment added |
| 11 | Redundant `ZERO_HEX_64` constant | kieran-typescript | Inlined |

Deferred to Phase B / operational: AppConfig type narrowing (Phase B consumers), key-rotation deletion runbook (operational), parser-duplication refactor (stylistic). Full artifact at `.context/compound-engineering/ce-review/20260513-212409-fdf79215/summary.md` (local-only per .gitignore).

## Summary

Adds a `<site-search>` Light-DOM custom element that filters the ~140 course / exercise / example / lecture pages client-side by title + meta description. Implements [#253](https://github.com/bushidocodes/limerick-cobol/issues/253).

- **Index builder** — `scripts/build-search-index.js` walks `course/`, `exercises/`, `examples/`, `lectures/`, pulls `<title>` and `<meta name=description>` out of each page, and writes `search-index.json` at the repo root (~32 KB, 138 entries). Wired up as `npm run build:search-index` and `check:search-index` (which is part of the aggregate `npm run check`).
- **Component** — `components/site-search.js` lazy-loads the JSON on first focus, scores entries (full-phrase title match > term in title > description > section), and renders a ranked dropdown. Auto-resolves the index URL from its own `<script src>`, so it works whether the host page is at depth 1 (`course/Selection.html`) or depth 2 (`examples/Accept/ACCEPT.html`).
- **Keyboard & a11y** — Cmd/Ctrl+K from any page focuses the input; ↑/↓/Home/End move the highlight; Enter navigates; Esc clears + closes. Wires an associated `<label>`, `role=combobox` / `listbox` / `option`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-activedescendant`, and an `aria-live` status announcer. `pa11y --standard WCAG2AA` returns "No issues found" on each page I checked.
- **Placement** — Rendered from inside `<page-hero>`, so the 107 lesson pages that already use the hero pick it up automatically. The 5 index/landing pages that don't use page-hero (root `index.html`, `course/index.html`, `exercises/index.html`, `examples/default.html`, `lectures/index.html`) got a manual `<site-search>` placement plus the `<script>` tag. Lecture leaf pages and the internal slideshow viewers under `course/Resources/ppz/` aren't wired up yet — they can follow in a separate sweep.
- **Styling** — New `.site-search*` rules in `course/Resources/css/course-components.css` use the existing CSS theme tokens (`--color-bg`, `--color-text`, `--color-border-mute`, `--color-emphasis`, …) so it inherits light and dark themes without extra work. A small `.visually-hidden` utility is added for the aria-live announcer.

No external dependencies — the scorer is ~30 lines of hand-rolled JS, in keeping with the no-build / no-runtime-deps stance of the rest of the site.

## Screenshots

The search field renders below the existing theme-toggle inside `<page-hero>`. On the index pages it sits below the page title, centered.

## Checklist

- [x] `npm run validate` passes
- [ ] `npm run links` — not run locally (port 8000 was busy); HTML output is identical to the originals plus the new `<site-search>` element and one extra `<script>` tag, so no links should have moved
- [x] `npm run format:check` passes on every file touched by this PR (pre-existing CRLF noise on untouched files is unchanged)
- [x] `npm run a11y` — `pa11y` run locally against the preview server on `index.html`, `course/index.html`, `course/Selection.html`, and `examples/Accept/ACCEPT.html`: "No issues found"

## Notes for reviewers

- `search-index.json` is committed, prettier-formatted, and gets regenerated by `npm run check` via `check:search-index` so it can't drift unnoticed.
- `MIN_QUERY` is 2 chars (issue text says "3+"); easy to bump to 3 if you'd prefer.
- The page-hero update is the load-bearing change — if the hero markup is reshuffled later, the search input goes with it.

body:
_Updated per addition of `for`, moved ARIA to core vs `HoverController`_

## Description

- Delivers the complete Phase 1 migration plan for `sp-tooltip` → `swc-tooltip`
- Documents the full 1st-gen API surface, all confirmed breaking changes, and all 2nd-gen API decisions
- Establishes the architecture (core vs SWC split), controller integration contracts, and migration checklist
- Resolves both planning questions (Q1: `tip-padding` dropped from 2nd-gen API surface; Q2: `popover="auto"` stack isolation accepted and documented as a known difference) and records four deferred implementation tickets
- Validates and documents `Element.ariaDescribedByElements` as the cross-root ARIA wiring strategy with a browser-support-confirmed POC

### Motivation and context

`sp-tooltip` is a visually simple component with significant behavioral complexity in its automatic trigger-wiring mode. This plan is the Phase 1 preparation artifact required before any implementation begins. It establishes what is in scope, what is deferred, what breaks for consumers, and what the implementation team needs to know before writing a line of code.

Key decisions recorded here:

**Six breaking changes (B1–B6):**

- B1: `slot="icon"` removed (S2 removes all icon rendering from Tooltip)
- B2: `variant="positive"` removed
- B3: `variant="info"` → `variant="informative"`
- B4: Logical placement values added (`start`, `end`, `start-top`, etc.) — TypeScript type widening only, not runtime-breaking
- B5: Event renames: `sp-opened`/`sp-closed` removed; 2nd-gen fires `swc-open`, `swc-after-open`, `swc-close`, `swc-after-close`. Event timing also changes due to native popover lifecycle; must document in consumer migration guide.
- B6: `self-managed` attribute removed; automatic trigger wiring is on by default; `manual` opts out; authoring pattern changes from nesting inside the trigger to sibling-after

**One a11y-critical fix (SWC-1558):** `role="tooltip"` is absent in 1st-gen and must ship in 2nd-gen.

**Infrastructure change:** `sp-overlay` dependency dropped entirely. 2nd-gen uses native `popover="auto"` + Floating UI per the Overlay Strategy RFC. `sp-overlay`, `DependencyManagerController`, and the `TooltipOpenable` internal element are all removed.

**Automatic trigger integration is additive:** The core tooltip (variants, CSS, `role="tooltip"`, popover open/close, event dispatch) can ship without prerequisites. ARIA relationship wiring via `for` / `trigger-element` is active from the initial release — the SWC layer sets `Element.ariaDescribedByElements` on `open` change in both automatic and manual modes. Hover/focus event wiring (`HoverController`) and pixel positioning (`PlacementController`) are deferred pending extraction of both controllers per the Overlay RFC.

**Cross-root ARIA wiring:** 2nd-gen button-like components render a semantic `<button>` inside shadow DOM. On `open` change, the SWC layer resolves the inner interactive element via `trigger.shadowRoot?.querySelector('button')` and sets `Element.ariaDescribedByElements = [tooltipHost]` on it — bypassing the cross-root ID-scoping limitation of string `aria-describedby`. Falls back to the trigger host for native elements and elements without an open shadow root. Validated with NVDA and VoiceOver across Chrome/Edge 135+, Firefox 136+, Safari 16.4+.

### Related issue(s)

- Epic SWC-2017 — Tooltip migration
- SWC-2019 (this ticket)

## Manual review test cases

- [ ] *Verify the six breaking changes are correctly characterized*
  1. Open [`CONTRIBUTOR-DOCS/.../tooltip/migration-plan.md`](CONTRIBUTOR-DOCS/03_project-planning/03_components/tooltip/migration-plan.md)
  2. Navigate to **Changes overview → Must ship**
  3. Confirm B1–B6 are documented with a clear consumer migration path for each
  4. Confirm that B4 (logical placements) is accurately framed as a TypeScript type-union change with no runtime breakage
  5. Confirm that B5 lists `swc-open`, `swc-after-open`, `swc-close`, `swc-after-close` as the four lifecycle events (no `swc-opened`/`swc-closed`)

- [ ] *Verify the 2nd-gen API decisions*
  1. Navigate to **2nd-gen API decisions → Public API**
  2. Verify the property table includes all confirmed attributes with correct types and defaults; additive/deferred properties are clearly marked
  3. Confirm `manual`, `labeling`, `trigger-element`, and `delayed` are present as additive/deferred with appropriate "ships inactive" notes
  4. Verify the visual matrix (variants, orientations) matches Figma references cited in the plan

- [ ] *Verify the controller integration contracts*
  1. Navigate to **Controller integration assumptions**
  2. Confirm `HoverController` hand-off is bounded: no trigger resolution inside the controller, no ARIA wiring inside the controller (ARIA wiring is owned by the SWC layer on `open` change), event dispatch stays in the `beforetoggle`/`toggle`/`transitionend` listeners, not the controller
  3. Confirm `PlacementController` hand-off is bounded: applies coordinates on `toggle`, no change to popover mechanism
  4. Confirm the `open` setter ↔ popover API cycle-prevention guard is documented

- [ ] *Verify the cross-root ARIA wiring rationale*
  1. Navigate to **Accessibility semantics notes → ARIA relationship wiring**
  2. Confirm the two resolution paths are specified: `trigger.shadowRoot.querySelector('button')` for SWC components; host element directly for native elements and elements without an open shadow root
  3. Confirm that ARIA wiring is driven by the SWC layer on `open` change — not by `HoverController`
  4. Confirm browser support details and POC CodePen link are present
  5. Confirm the prohibition on string-ID `aria-describedby` as a fallback is explicit

- [ ] *Verify the authoring modes section*
  1. Navigate to **2nd-gen API decisions → Behavioral semantics → Authoring modes**
  2. Confirm all four Mode 1 variants are present: native trigger, `swc-action-button` with text, icon-only with `accessible-label` (preferred), icon-only with `labeling` attribute (additive)
  3. Confirm Mode 2 (explicit `trigger-element`) and Mode 3 (`manual`) are present, syntactically correct, and annotated appropriately

- [ ] *Verify resolved questions and deferred tickets*
  1. Navigate to **Blockers and open questions**
  2. Confirm Q1 (`tip-padding`) is marked resolved: dropped from the 2nd-gen API surface; `arrowPadding` is a `PlacementController` concern for Popover/CoachMark
  3. Confirm Q2 (`popover="auto"` stack isolation) is marked resolved with Path A accepted: behavior is documented as a known difference from 1st-gen, not a bug
  4. Confirm the four deferred implementation tickets are present with summaries, deferral rationale, and correct additive section references (PlacementController → A1/A7/A8/A9; HoverController → A1/A2/A3/A4; tooltip-directive → A6; no-tip → A5)

## Summary
Two gaps surfaced during end-to-end testing of \`ANcpLua.NET.Sdk.BitNet\` from nuget.org:

1. The README lists \`.NET.Sdk\`, \`.Web\`, and \`.Test\` variants but never mentions \`ANcpLua.NET.Sdk.BitNet\` (on nuget.org since 3.4.x) and never names \`ANcpLua.Agents.Hosting.BitNet\` as the implicit injection.
2. Every variant forces \`ManagePackageVersionsCentrally=true\` (Common.props line 47) and Enforcement.props errors if a consumer disables it — but the Quick Start makes no mention of the CPM contract. A first-time consumer doing \`Sdk=\"ANcpLua.NET.Sdk.BitNet\"\` without a \`Directory.Packages.props\` hits a confusing \`NU1015\` on the SDK-injected analyzers (which switch to \`GlobalPackageReference\` under CPM).

- New "**BitNet variant — what it adds**" subsection names the implicit \`ANcpLua.Agents.Hosting.BitNet\` PackageReference, links the hosting-package README for the four wiring modes (zero-config / named-connection / programmatic / source-generator), and explains the version-lockstep contract with ANcpLua/ANcpLua.Agents.
- Bumped example versions from 3.4.21 → 3.4.31 (latest published).

## How it was verified
- Reproduced \`NU1015\` failure in a clean-room consumer without \`Directory.Packages.props\` (Sdk=\"ANcpLua.NET.Sdk.BitNet\" 3.4.31, no Directory.Packages.props in tree).

body:
## Problem

Two CI runs on main failed with a 90 s `beforeAll` timeout — alternating which test file timed out — on an underpowered runner. The root cause is unresolved: we don't yet know whether opencode is slow to start or slow to respond once started.

## What this does

Adds `AbortSignal.timeout` to both unbounded `fetch` calls in `waitFor` and `sendPromptAndWait`. Without this, a fetch that connects but gets no response hangs indefinitely, causing `beforeAll` to block until bun's 90 s hook timeout fires with no diagnostic output.

Also streams opencode's stderr live and adds step checkpoints so the CI log shows exactly where execution stalls.

body:
## Summary

PR 2 of the 3-part Stripe Customer Portal rollout. Ships two new on-site legal pages so the Stripe Portal footer can link to real rubberfit URLs.

- `src/app/legal/privacy/page.tsx` — Privacy Policy (10 numbered sections + sub-processors and retention tables + CCPA notice)
- `src/app/legal/terms/page.tsx` — Terms of Service (15 numbered sections; Nevada governing law)
- `SubPage` gains optional `hideCtaSection?: boolean` prop — legal pages opt out of the "Start a trial" CTA; default behavior unchanged for the 8 existing callers
- Footer: replaces the off-site `docs.rubberfit.app/security/data-handling` "Privacy policy" link with on-site `/legal/privacy`; adds `/legal/terms`
- Sitemap: adds both routes
- New CSS: `.legal-layout` (responsive grid with sticky desktop TOC), `.legal-section` (scroll-margin so anchored sections clear the sticky nav), `.legal-body`, `.legal-list`, `.legal-table`, `.sr-only`

## Design

Authored by Kimi K2.6 from a written design brief. Two-column layout with a sticky desktop TOC + flat mobile chip TOC; numbered `§NN` section anchors using existing design tokens (`--color-signal-deep`, `--color-rule`, `--font-mono`, `--font-display`). No "Start a trial" CTA on legal pages — the closing block is a quiet mono footer (effective date + contact + jurisdiction).

## Review gates

- `pnpm lint` clean
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` clean
- `pnpm build` clean — 16 static routes (was 14); `/legal/privacy` + `/legal/terms` both ○ static
- `code-reviewer` subagent — 3 IMPORTANT (sticky-nav scroll-margin clipping, `!important` grid override, IO-observer flicker on multi-entry batches) all fixed; 7 NITs (aria-current, table scope+caption, nav aria-label, motion.section semantic upgrade applied; TOC component dedupe + sitemap-priority deferred)
- `codex review` — P0 untracked `/legal/` files (procedural, included in this commit) + 2 P2 a11y (both applied)
- `coderabbit review --plain --type committed --base origin/init` — no findings ✔

## Founder action items (after merge)

1. **Skim the legal copy.** The Privacy Policy and Terms are starter / template copy adapted from `docs.rubberfit.app/security/data-handling` and standard SaaS terms with Nevada governing law (matching the Arc & Anchor LV address). Recommend a quick read; counsel review is sensible but not blocking the Portal use case.
2. **Run the Stripe Portal config patch** to point the footer links at the new pages:
   ```bash

   curl -X POST "https://api.stripe.com/v1/billing_portal/configurations/bpc_1TWh902OM4DE2aIIyE4cpiOG" \
     -u "${KEY}:" \
     -d "business_profile[privacy_policy_url]=https://get.rubberfit.app/legal/privacy" \
   ```

author: hoangtrungnguyen
body:
## Summary

Adds non-fatal calls to `grava_plane_sync.py` in three coding-team agents (`coder`, `reviewer`, `pr-creator`) immediately after every signal emission. Implements the **v0 per-agent-hook approach** described in stellar-engine's [`docs/grava-plane-status-sync-plan.md`](https://github.com/hoangtrungnguyen/stellar-engine/blob/main/docs/grava-plane-status-sync-plan.md).

## Why

When the grava coding team transitions an issue's state (CODER_DONE, REVIEWER_APPROVED, PR_DONE, …), the linked Plane work item's status should follow automatically. Today nothing pushes those transitions to Plane. This PR adds the hook points; the sync helper script itself lands separately in stellar-engine.

## What changed

- `.claude/agents/coder.md` — hook after `CODER_DONE` and `CODER_HALTED`.
- `.claude/agents/reviewer.md` — hook after `REVIEWER_APPROVED` and `REVIEWER_BLOCKED`.
- `.claude/agents/pr-creator.md` — hooks on success path, on `finalize-pr.sh` failure, and on pre-flight failure paths.

All invocations:

```bash
python3 "${STELLAR_ENGINE_HOME:-/Users/trungnguyenhoang/IdeaProjects/stellar-engine}/agents/task-generator/cli/grava_plane_sync.py" \
    "$ISSUE_ID" \
    --project-id "${PLANE_PROJECT_ID:-…}" \
    --grava-repo "${GRAVA_REPO:-/Users/trungnguyenhoang/IdeaProjects/grava}" \
    --system-yaml "${STELLAR_ENGINE_HOME:-…}/systems/SportBuddies/system.yaml" \
    || true
```

The `|| true` is load-bearing — sync failure must never block the pipeline.

## What reviewers should know

- **The helper script does not exist yet.** `agents/task-generator/cli/grava_plane_sync.py` is not present in stellar-engine `main` at the time of this PR. With `|| true`, the hook silently no-ops until the script lands. This is intentional per the v0 plan: ship the hook points first, ship the helper second.
- **Hard-coded fallback paths** to `/Users/trungnguyenhoang/IdeaProjects/stellar-engine` and `/Users/trungnguyenhoang/IdeaProjects/grava` only apply when `STELLAR_ENGINE_HOME` / `GRAVA_REPO` are unset. Documented in the upstream sync plan §Risks (path coupling).
- **Project ID and system.yaml path are SportBuddies-specific** in the fallback. Operators on a different system override via `PLANE_PROJECT_ID` env var and a different `--system-yaml`.
- All three modified files agree on the env var precedence pattern; no behavioral drift between them.

## Test plan

- [ ] With `STELLAR_ENGINE_HOME` unset and the helper script absent: trigger `CODER_DONE`; confirm the pipeline completes cleanly (sync silently no-ops, agent exits as before).
- [ ] With the helper script present (once it lands): trigger `CODER_DONE` on a Plane-linked grava issue; confirm the Plane work item's state transitions.
- [ ] Confirm `REVIEWER_BLOCKED` and `CODER_HALTED` paths also call the sync.
- [ ] Inspect `pr-creator.md` finalize-pr.sh failure path: PR_FAILED signal emitted, sync attempted, exit 1 preserved.

The CI Tests workflow only runs lint and tests. It doesn't open issues, push commits, attach release artifacts, or invoke OIDC. Right now it inherits whatever `permissions:` the repo default grants the workflow token.

This patch sets `permissions: contents: read` at the workflow level so the scope is documented in-file and stays the minimum required by `actions/checkout`. publish-nightly.yml and publish-release.yml already declare job-level permission blocks (id-token: write for trusted publishing); applying the analogous read-only pattern to ci.yaml closes the gap.

No new dependencies, no behavioural change.

author: furkankoykiran
body:
Brings the setup in line with [Anthropic's CLAUDE.md best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices). Quoting the relevant guidance:

> Target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file. Longer files consume more context and **reduce adherence**.
>
> Bloated CLAUDE.md files cause Claude to ignore your actual instructions!
>
> For domain knowledge or workflows that are only relevant sometimes, **use skills instead**. Claude loads them on demand without bloating every conversation.
>
> Splitting into `@path` imports helps organization but **does not reduce context**, since imported files load at launch.

## Before / after

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| CLAUDE.md size | 105 lines / ~1,840 tokens | 94 lines / ~1,824 tokens |
| `@`-imported docs | 5 files / ~4,600 tokens | 0 |
| **Total session-start load** | **~6,440 tokens** | **~1,824 tokens (-72%)** |
| Broken `@RTK.md` import | yes | fixed |

## What got pruned and why

- **`docs/github-workflow.md` (180 lines, ~1,650 tokens)** — 80% was a reference catalog of `mcp__github__*` tool names and `gh` bash examples that Claude rediscovers on demand. Kept only the 6 load-bearing rules inline (MCP first, DCO, no AI attribution, human-toned comments, efficient server-side filtering).
- **`docs/mcp-reference.md` (44 lines)** — the entire file boiled down to one rule about `-e` flag ordering, now one line in CLAUDE.md.
- **`docs/agents-reference.md` (35 lines)** — agent triggers are already in CLAUDE.md; the file was just a duplicate "when to spawn" table.
- **`docs/skills-reference.md` (46 lines)** — Claude auto-discovers skills via the registry. Only kept the few selection rules that aren't obvious (e.g., "always use `/browse`, never `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`").
- **`docs/karpathy-guidelines.md` (79 lines, added 2 PRs ago)** — folded into a unified "Coding Discipline" section in CLAUDE.md so it doesn't duplicate the existing Approach Rules. Same content, half the tokens.
- **`docs/gstack-use-cases.md` (365 lines)** — wasn't actually `@`-imported (only a plain markdown link from `skills-reference.md`), so it was dead weight on disk. Removed.

## CLAUDE.md changes

- **Merged "Approach Rules" + "Coding Discipline (Karpathy)"** into one section. They overlapped on plan-before-executing / address-root-causes; kept the additive Karpathy rules (simplicity first, surgical changes, goal-driven execution).
- **Inlined the rules** from each deleted doc; removed catalog/reference content Claude rediscovers on demand.
- **Cut "Code Style Adaptation" entirely** — "read existing code before writing new code" is Claude's default; the section was just talk.
- **Compressed "Testing & Code Quality"** from 9 bullets to 6 — dropped items Claude derives from lock files (e.g., "Python uses pytest/ruff/mypy").
- **Removed broken `@RTK.md` import** — file never existed; rtk wires its hook via `settings.json` from `install.sh`.

## Dependent fixes

- `skills/find-repos/SKILL.md`, `skills/solve-issue/SKILL.md`, `skills/pr-followup/SKILL.md` — replaced now-broken `@docs/github-workflow.md` reference with a one-sentence rule.
- `install.sh` — corrected a misleading log line that claimed rtk's `--hook-only` flag "skips RTK.md/CLAUDE.md" (it only writes settings.json).
- `README.md` — Layout section no longer claims `RTK.md` exists or that `docs/` holds imported references.

## Verification

```
$ wc -l CLAUDE.md
94 CLAUDE.md
$ grep -rn '@docs/' --include='*.md' --include='*.sh' .
(no results)
$ grep -rn '@RTK.md' .
(no results)
```

author: appsecai-app[bot]
body:
## What we found **Vulnerabilities:** 3 instances of CWE-326 (Inadequate Encryption) **Severity:** Medium **File:** `src/main/java/org/owasp/benchmark/testcode/BenchmarkTest00210.java` **Affected Lines:** 77, 80 (multiple detections) **Detected By:** OpenGrep **Detection Rules:** - `java.lang.security.audit.crypto.des-is-deprecated` (lines 77, 80) - `java.lang.security.audit.crypto.desede-is-deprecated` (line 80) **Description:** The code uses DES (Data Encryption Standard) and DESede (3DES) for encryption operations. Both algorithms are cryptographically broken and deprecated by NIST since 2005. DES uses only a 56-bit effective key length, making it vulnerable to brute-force attacks with modern hardware. The vulnerable code instantiates `Cipher.getInstance("DES/CBC/PKCS5Padding")` and `KeyGenerator.getInstance("DES")` to encrypt security-sensitive data (passwords) persisted to `passwordFile.txt`. ## Why this matters **Risk if not fixed:** An attacker with access to encrypted data can recover the plaintext using brute-force key enumeration. DES's 56-bit key space can be exhausted in hours on commodity hardware or minutes on specialized equipment. This directly compromises the confidentiality of passwords and other secrets encrypted with DES. **Risk level:** Medium — Should be addressed in regular security maintenance. The servlet endpoint `/crypto-00/BenchmarkTest00210` is publicly accessible, making the vulnerable encryption reachable by any HTTP client without authentication. **Impact:** Encrypted passwords stored in `passwordFile.txt` are not protected against determined attackers. Compliance frameworks (PCI-DSS, HIPAA, SOC 2) explicitly prohibit DES for protecting sensitive data. ## Why we're changing it **Status:** Confirmed vulnerability **Evidence:** - Line 77: `Cipher.getInstance("DES/CBC/PKCS5Padding")` — hardcoded DES algorithm with no conditional guards or suppression comments - Line 80: `KeyGenerator.getInstance("DES").generateKey()` — DES key generation confirmed - Lines 102–111: Encrypted ciphertext written to `passwordFile.txt` — security-sensitive context established - Line 27: Servlet mapped at `/crypto-00/BenchmarkTest00210` with no authentication guards — sink reachable by any HTTP client - DES formally withdrawn by NIST in 2005; cryptanalysis has been public since the late 1990s **Remediation approach:** Replace DES with AES (Advanced Encryption Standard), which uses a 128-bit key (or larger) and is approved by NIST SP 800-131A Rev 2. Preserve CBC mode and PKCS5Padding to maintain functional equivalence with existing code paths. ## How we confirmed **Automated checks we ran:** - Static pattern matching: OpenGrep detected hardcoded `"DES"` and `"DESede"` algorithm strings - Syntax and semantic validation: Java code compiles without errors - Import verification: `javax.crypto.Cipher` and `javax.crypto.KeyGenerator` are standard JDK classes **LLM review of the diff:** - Functional review: AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding is a drop-in replacement for DES/CBC/PKCS5Padding in this context - Code quality review: IV length adjustment (8 → 16 bytes) is correct for AES block size - Security review: No new vulnerabilities introduced; all three DES/DESede references eliminated **Reachability analysis:** The servlet endpoint `/crypto-00/BenchmarkTest00210` is publicly accessible via HTTP. Every request to this endpoint unconditionally executes the vulnerable code path: 1. HTTP request arrives at `doPost()` method 2. Custom header value is extracted 3. Line 74: IV is generated (8 bytes for DES, now 16 for AES) 4. Line 77: Cipher instantiated with weak algorithm 5. Line 80: Key generated with weak algorithm 6. Plaintext encrypted and written to file No conditional guards, authentication checks, or feature flags prevent execution of the vulnerable sink. ### Vulnerability Flow Diagram ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme':'base','themeVariables':{'fontFamily':'ui-sans-serif, Inter, system-ui, sans-serif','primaryColor':'#EDE9FE','primaryTextColor':'#1A1A2E','primaryBorderColor':'#7C3AED','lineColor':'#5B21B6','secondaryColor':'#FEF3C7','tertiaryColor':'#DCFCE7'}}}%% flowchart TD A["HTTP Request

8 bytes for DES"] C --> D["Line 77 - Cipher.getInstance
DES/CBC/PKCS5Padding"] D --> E["Line 80 - KeyGenerator.getInstance
DES - 56-bit key"] E --> F["❌ Encrypt with Weak Key
2^56 key space"] F --> G["Write to passwordFile.txt
Brute-force feasible"] H["✅ Fixed - AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding
128-bit key, 16-byte IV"] -.-> I["2^128 key space
Brute-force infeasible"] style D fill:#FFE5E5,stroke:#F65A5A style E fill:#FFE5E5,stroke:#F65A5A style F fill:#FEF3C7,stroke:#F59E0B style G fill:#FEF3C7,stroke:#F59E0B style H fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A style I fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A ``` ### Vulnerable flow: src/main/java/org/owasp/benchmark/testcode/BenchmarkTest00210.java:77 _Weak Encryption Algorithm_ ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme':'base','themeVariables':{'fontFamily':'ui-sans-serif, Inter, system-ui, sans-serif','primaryColor':'#EDE9FE','primaryTextColor':'#1A1A2E','primaryBorderColor':'#7C3AED','lineColor':'#5B21B6','secondaryColor':'#FEF3C7','tertiaryColor':'#DCFCE7'}}}%% flowchart TD subgraph Vulnerable["❌ Vulnerable Flow — DES/CBC/PKCS5Padding"] direction LR A1["HTTP Request
Custom Header"] --> A2["BenchmarkTest00210
doPost()"] A2 --> A3["KeyGenerator.getInstance

2^56 key space"] end Vulnerable ~~~ Fixed subgraph Fixed["✅ Fixed Flow — AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding"] direction LR B1["HTTP Request

doPost()"] B2 --> B3["KeyGenerator.getInstance
AES — 128-bit key"] B3 --> B4["Cipher.getInstance

### Motivation
- Provide shortcode-based UI for wallet-driven booking gating, conditional content, and balance display in a secure, sanitized way.

author: rodrigoi
body:
## Problem

The `ph livestream` command only outputs JSON lines, which is useful for scripting but not for interactive exploration. Users watching live events want a visual interface similar to the Go-based livestream TUI.

## Changes

**New TUI mode (`cli-2.0/src/livestream/tui/`)**

Added an interactive terminal interface using Ink (React for CLI):

- **App.tsx**: Main application component managing modes (events list, event detail, help overlay, filter input).
- **Header.tsx**: Shows team name, connection status, and active filters.
- **StatsBar.tsx**: Displays event counts and streaming stats.
- **EventsTable.tsx**: Scrollable list of events with keyboard navigation.
- **EventDetail.tsx**: JSON viewer for selected event with j/k scrolling.
- **Footer.tsx**: Context-sensitive keyboard shortcuts.
- **HelpOverlay.tsx**: Full keybinding reference.
- **FilterInput.tsx**: Input modal for event type and distinct ID filters.

**Hooks (`cli-2.0/src/livestream/tui/hooks/`)**

- **useEventStream.ts**: Manages SSE connection, reconnection, and event buffering.

**Mode selection (`cli-2.0/src/livestream/index.ts`)**

- TUI mode is default when stdout is a TTY.
- JSON mode via `--json` flag or when piping output.
- Graceful degradation: non-TTY environments automatically use JSON mode.

**Keyboard shortcuts**

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `j/k` or arrows | Navigate events |
| `Enter` | View event detail |
| `p` | Pause/resume stream |
| `f` | Filter by event type |
| `d` | Filter by distinct ID |
| `x` | Clear filters |
| `?` | Show help |
| `q` | Quit |

**Dependencies added**

- `ink` and `ink-spinner` for TUI rendering.
- `react` and `@types/react` (Ink is React-based).

## How did you test this code?

**Manual testing**

```bash
# Build
pnpm --filter=@posthog/cli-2.0 build

# TUI mode (default)
ph livestream

# JSON mode
ph livestream --json

# With filters
ph livestream --event-type '$pageview'
ph livestream --distinct-id 'user123'

# Piped output (auto JSON)
ph livestream | head -5
```

Verified:
- Events stream in real-time.
- Navigation with j/k and arrows.
- Detail view shows full event JSON.
- Filters apply correctly.
- Pause/resume works.
- Quit exits cleanly.
- Non-TTY environments fall back to JSON.

![cat-type-small](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79a1b6e0-5095-4395-930c-348c9589f538)

## Publish to changelog?

No - hackathon project, not yet ready for changelog.

## 🤖 Agent context

Co-authored with Claude Code (Opus 4.5).

**Approach**:
- Ported the visual design from the Go TUI (`livestream/tui/`) to Ink/React.
- Used functional components with hooks for state management.
- Separated concerns: streaming logic in hooks, rendering in components.

**Key decisions**:
- Used `ink-spinner` for loading states instead of custom animation.
- Stored selected event object (not index) in detail view to prevent content shifting as new events arrive.
- Added `process.exit(0)` on quit since Ink's `exit()` alone doesn't terminate when SSE streams are active.
- Changed Footer's `key` prop to `hotkey` since `key` is reserved by React.

author: douglas125
body:
## Summary

Fixes two issues from the prod team-analysis run that ended *"Currently the"*:

1. **The cut-off wasn't Discord — it was the model's `max_tokens=1500` cap.** Lowered to **1000** (~4000 chars; comfortable margin under Discord's 6000-char total embed limit). Prompt now explicitly targets **under 250 words** and tells the agent that a team analysis is a verdict + 3-6 bullets, not a per-unit essay.
2. **`stop_reason='max_tokens'` was treated as an opaque error.** Now flagged as a soft truncation: partial answer is preserved, footer says \`truncated (max output tokens)\`. Iteration cap still distinguished as \`truncated (iteration cap)\`.

Plus a caching upgrade per [the docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching):

3. **Switched to top-level `cache_control={"type":"ephemeral","ttl":"1h"}`** on \`messages.create\` (SDK's "auto caching"). The breakpoint now moves to the last cacheable block on every iteration, so iteration N+1 reads the entire iteration-N prefix from cache instead of re-paying for it. The explicit \`cache_control\` on the system block was removed — having both would burn one of the four allowed breakpoints for no benefit.

   Expected impact on multi-iteration runs: per-iteration uncached tokens drop from "system + tools + full history" to "just the latest tool_result + assistant turn". The 333K-token / \$0.28 prod run from earlier should drop substantially.

## Test plan

- [x] \`pytest tests/test_bot_ask_ai.py\` — 42 passed (added \`test_loop_flags_max_tokens_as_truncated\`, \`test_embed_footer_max_tokens_truncated_label\`; existing \`test_loop_returns_text_on_end_turn\` now also asserts \`cache_control\` is on the top-level kwargs and absent from system blocks).
- [x] Full suite: 541 passed.
- [ ] **After Railway deploy:** re-run the team-analysis question; answer should be ≤250 words, footer should NOT say \"truncated\". Per-iteration token growth in \`ai_queries\` should be much smaller than the previous 200K+ runs.

author: chanyavrc
body:
## Summary

- Added thread-local re-entrancy guards (`REPR_IN_PROGRESS`, `EQ_IN_PROGRESS`) modelled on CPython's `Py_ReprEnter`/`Py_ReprLeave`; recursive `Value::repr` on a self-referential `List` / `Dict` / `Set` / `Tuple` now emits the CPython placeholder (`[...]` / `{...}` / `(...)`) instead of blowing the stack.
- `PartialEq for Value` tracks the ordered pair of `value_id()`s currently being compared and short-circuits to `true` on re-entry, matching CPython's "the prefix has already been proven equal" cycle semantics, so `a == a` (and `a == b` on two distinct cycles) no longer aborts the process.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --all`
- [x] `cargo test --release --bin pyrust` (272 passed)
- [x] `cargo test --release --test parity_compare` (1 passed, all `.py` cases)
- [x] `cargo test -p pyrust-derive --test trybuild` (1 passed)
- [x] New parity case `crates/pyrust/tests/cases/runtime/test_cyclic_repr.py` covers `repr` / `str` / `print` / `==` of a self-referential dict and a nested cycle.
- [x] Microbench (`repr([1..10]) x 100k`): ~1% wall-clock regression vs. baseline, well under the 5% threshold.

Closes #364.

## Summary

- Introduces `RecordingCoordinator` — a shared state machine that serialises all recording-lifecycle transitions (`Idle → Recording → Transcribing/PostProcessing → Idle`)
- Fixes the core bug where pressing the shortcut always emitted `RecordingStarted` regardless of current state; second press now correctly stops recording and begins transcription
- `ShortcutManager` and `ipc_dispatch_loop` now call coordinator methods (`toggle`, `toggle_with_post_process`, `start_ptt`, `stop_ptt`, `cancel`) instead of emitting raw `BackendEvent`s directly
- Push-to-talk key-down/key-up is correctly handled for both the primary and post-process shortcuts
- `cancel()` aborts any in-flight state (Recording, Transcribing, PostProcessing) and returns to Idle
- Also fixes `.gitignore`: the `recording_*` pattern (intended for audio files) was blocking the new `.rs` source file; added `!recording_*.rs` negation

body:
## Summary

- **Introduces `assistant_os/mso/perception.py`** with `build_economic_perception_frame()` — a bounded, read-only frame that assembles live system state for the MSO cognitive path without increasing LLM call count.
- **Delegates `build_mso_grounding_context()`** in `narrative_runtime.py` to the new frame, preserving Phase 1 backward compat via a `pending_review_items` alias.
- **Expands `build_mso_chat_system_prompt()`** in `prompts.py` to render 5 structured sections (capabilities, prepared actions, governance decisions, active tasks, recent failures) with explicit "No data currently visible." fallbacks and a `PERCEPTION WARNINGS` block.

## What Changed

### `assistant_os/mso/perception.py` (new)
- `build_economic_perception_frame() -> dict` — assembles 21 fields from 6 subsystem reads
- Every read is wrapped in `try/except`; failures append to `perception_warnings` and return safe defaults
- `execution_allowed=False`, `can_execute_now=False`, `execution_closed=True` are hardcoded at the return site — never derived from any subsystem
- Bounded to 5 items per list source (`_MAX_ITEMS = 5`)
- `session_history` deferred: `session_history_available=False`, `session_history=[]`

### `assistant_os/mso/narrative_runtime.py`
- `build_mso_grounding_context()` reduced from 61 lines to 9 — thin delegator to `build_economic_perception_frame()`
- Adds `pending_review_items` alias for Phase 1 callers
- All other functions (`is_mso_narrative_intent`, `build_narrative_context_message`) unchanged

### `assistant_os/mso/prompts.py`
- `build_mso_chat_system_prompt()` now renders capabilities, prepared actions, governance decisions, active tasks, and recent failures from the frame
- Sections render "No data currently visible." when empty — LLM cannot fill in absent data
- HARD RULES updated: model instructed not to invent capabilities, tasks, failures, or governance not present in the frame
- Execution boundary explicit in prompt: `execution_allowed=false, can_execute_now=false`

## Test Results

| Suite | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_economic_perception.py` | — | **37 / 37** |
| `test_surface_behavior_layer.py` | 133 / 133 | **142 / 142** (+9 Phase 2) |
| `test_ui_runtime_truth_contracts.py` | 381 / 381 | **381 / 381** |
| **Total** | 514 | **560 / 560** |

No UI files changed — Vitest / TypeScript not required.

## Reviewer Notes

- **No authority chain, Police, or Machine Operator files were touched.** Confirmed by diff and by an AST-based test (`test_perception_module_does_not_import_forbidden_modules`) that verifies `perception.py` does not import any forbidden modules.
- **Alpha Phase 1 provenance is fully preserved.** `response_source`, `execution_status`, `cognitive_trace`, `raw_response` behavior is unchanged. Regression-tested by `test_alpha1_provenance_fields_not_regressed`.
- **Session history is intentionally deferred.** No session store exists in the current architecture. The frame signals this explicitly with `session_history_available=False` so the LLM knows rather than inventing history.
- **`pending_review_items` alias.** The old key still present in every grounding context dict to avoid breaking any callers that were written against Phase 1 contracts.

## Files Changed

```
assistant_os/mso/perception.py               (new)
assistant_os/mso/narrative_runtime.py        (modified: -61/+9 lines)
assistant_os/mso/prompts.py                  (modified: +120 lines)
tests/test_economic_perception.py            (new, 37 tests)
```

## Summary

First slice of M2 — close the transparency gap where users couldn't read their own audit-log rows.

- New MCP tool ``get_my_audit_log(limit, before)`` — newest-first, limit clamp [1,500] default 50.

body:
## Summary

Cross-page audit on the 6 project case studies found **19 em-dashes** in `projects.ts`. Calvin's standing instruction is "no em/en dashes that are unnecessary." 13 were rhetorical / parenthetical em-dashes in prose that have cleaner alternatives.

## What I replaced

| Pattern | Replacement | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Parenthetical em-dash pair around inline list | Parentheses | "Everything that follows (the persona model, the consent flow, the six scenarios) comes from that premise." |
| Em-dash separating two independent clauses | Period | "Companion lives where the files already do. The moment it becomes a separate app, it inherits the upload chore..." |
| Em-dash introducing a definition / restatement | Colon | "...lowering search costs at every turn: visual instead of textual, grouped instead of listed..." |

13 edits across Drive Companion, Music Pathways, and Matchify case studies. Anatomy of Fear and Night Shift were already clean. Tutorly had none.

## What I kept (justified)

- **Line 507**: `"Welcome — I'm Jay!"` is quoted UI copy from the original Music Pathways chatbot — preserving the literal greeting
- **All en-dashes inside numeric ranges** (`0–1`, `75–90%`, `0.3–0.5`) — typographically correct for ranges and removing them would make rubric values look like item IDs
- **All Unicode minuses in negative correlations** (`−0.34`, `−0.245`) — clearly distinguishes negative numbers from hyphens in the stats / data prose

## Audit result on other consistency dimensions

- ✅ All 6 projects have stats (4 each), pull quote, key findings, features, tools, impact, limitations
- ✅ All features and visualizations have `insight` fields
- ✅ Image conventions are consistent within each project (anatomy/drive/music/night-shift use landscape `imageFit: 'contain'`; matchify and tutorly use `phoneFrame: true` mobile portraits)
- ⚠️ **Anatomy of Fear is the only project without a `decisions` chapter** — left unchanged because I don't have Calvin's actual product decisions for that project; inventing them would be worse than the asymmetry
- ⚠️ Matchify and Tutorly intentionally don't set a top-level `image:` (portrait mobile UI doesn't fit the 16:9 hero slot) — same call I made when those were rewritten

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` compiles cleanly (all 6 project pages prerendered)
- [x] `grep "—"` returns only the one justified instance in line 507
- [ ] Visual QA: read each project's overview / motivation / decisions / impact and confirm the prose flows naturally without the em-dashes

body:
## Summary

Whole-app pass against the punchlist:

### Overlay & window
- Replaced dokar3 `BottomSheetLayout` with a custom 4-detent sheet: **HIDDEN / PEEK / HALF / FULL**.
- `LogKittyOverlayService` now sizes the WindowManager view to match the active detent and sets `FLAG_NOT_TOUCH_MODAL`, so taps outside the sheet always reach the underlying app. The system overlay no longer steals touches across the screen.
- FULL height = 90% of screen — the log display extends down to the bottom-10% mark.
- HIDDEN leaves only a 14dp swipe-up/tap grab strip at the bottom.

### Gestures
- Header (handle + tabs + icon row): vertical drag steps the detent up/down, horizontal drag flips tabs.
- Log area: vertical drag scrolls the LazyColumn, horizontal drag flips tabs.
- Thin **2dp** drag handle replaces the chunky 6dp pill.

### Tabs
- System, Errors, and one per foreground-app captured by the accessibility service.
- The close-`X` only appears on the **selected** APP tab.
- Side-swipe navigates between tabs in both PEEK and HALF/FULL detents.

### Icon-bar buttons
- **X**: first press clears the active tab only (per-tab marker via `IndexedLogLine` ids — other tabs keep their history). Second press within 3s collapses the sheet to HIDDEN.
- **Save** and **Settings**: hide the sheet to HIDDEN first, then launch their action.
- Back key collapses HALF/FULL → HIDDEN; a second back propagates to the app below (window is only focusable in HALF/FULL).
- Home/Recents collapse via accessibility broadcast — the system performs the navigation as usual.

### Log entries
- Tap a line to select; toolbar above the log offers **Copy / Search (Google) / Prohibit**.
- Prohibit extracts the tag and adds it to the persisted block-list.
- Prohibited list manager is now reachable from Settings (was orphan UI before).

### Color schemes
- Six built-in schemes — **Material (default), Android Studio, Pidcat, Monochrome, Solarized, Custom**.
- Tag-based coloring for common Android components (toggleable).
- Per-level color editor (any edit auto-switches the active scheme to CUSTOM).
- All preferences persist via SharedPreferences and are covered by `backup_rules.xml` / `data_extraction_rules.xml` (already in place).
- New **Export Preferences** / **Import Preferences** entries in Settings (SAF + clipboard fallback).

### Misc
- Removed the dead `sendPrompt` AI placeholder.
- Bumped `version.properties` to 0.6.0.
- Updated `docs/file_descriptions.md` and `docs/TODO.md`.

## Test plan
- [ ] PEEK → swipe up to HALF, then up to FULL; swipe down through PEEK to HIDDEN.
- [ ] In HIDDEN, swipe up or tap the thin strip to return to PEEK.
- [ ] HALF or FULL: tap outside the sheet — touches must hit the app behind it.
- [ ] Side-swipe inside any non-HIDDEN detent switches tabs.
- [ ] Open an app, confirm a tab appears; select it; verify close-X appears only on the selected APP tab and removing the tab does not affect System/Errors.
- [ ] Press X — only the active tab's logs disappear. Press X again within 3s — sheet hides.
- [ ] Save & Settings — sheet hides before action.
- [ ] Back key in HALF/FULL hides the sheet; second back goes to the app.
- [ ] Home / Recents from any expanded detent — sheet hides immediately and the system action proceeds.
- [ ] Tap a log line — Copy / Search / Prohibit toolbar appears. Verify each action.
- [ ] Settings → Color Scheme → switch through all six. Customize one level and verify scheme flips to Custom.
- [ ] Settings → Export Preferences → saves JSON. Re-import — values restored.
- [ ] Verify ProhibitedLogsScreen lists prohibited tags and the remove button works.
- [ ] `./gradlew assembleDebug` (sandbox here lacks network for the foojay plugin — please run in CI).

author: moon345x
body:
# PR: ES-49 — Explicador de Errores

## 📋 Historia de Usuario

> **Como desarrollador**, quiero que la IA analice los errores de salida de la terminal, **para** entender rápidamente la causa de un fallo y recibir una propuesta de solución.

***

## ✅ Criterios de Aceptación

- [x] Botón **"Preguntar a Pro-Tocol"** aparece en la terminal cuando un comando devuelve exit code != 0.
- [x] El stack de error completo (stdout + stderr del comando fallido) es enviado automáticamente a la IA para diagnóstico.

***

## 🔧 Cambios Realizados

### `lib/logic/terminal_command_tracker.dart` *(nuevo)*
- Clase `TerminalCommandTracker` que intercepta el stream SSH a nivel de capa de transporte.
- Inyecta el sentinel `echo "__PROTO_EXIT__:$?"` automáticamente después de cada `Enter` enviado al shell interactivo.
- Parsea el stream de stdout buscando el patrón `__PROTO_EXIT__:<code>` para detectar exit code != 0.
- Expone `ValueNotifier<String?> lastFailedOutput` con el output capturado del comando fallido.
- Método `filterStdoutForDisplay(Uint8List bytes)` que elimina las líneas del sentinel **antes** de que lleguen al widget xterm — el usuario nunca ve `__PROTO_EXIT__:1` en pantalla.

### `lib/view/pages/server_tabs/TerminalTab.dart`
- Recibe el `TerminalCommandTracker` como dependencia.
- Escucha `tracker.lastFailedOutput` con un `ValueListenableBuilder`.
- Cuando hay un fallo activo, muestra un `AnimatedSwitcher` con un banner **"Preguntar a Pro-Tocol"** superpuesto en la parte inferior del terminal.
- El banner se descarta automáticamente cuando el usuario ejecuta el siguiente comando exitoso.

### `lib/view/pages/server_tabs/ChatIaTab.dart`
- Añadido `ChatIaController` con una cola (`Queue<String>`) de prompts programáticos.
- Método público `injectErrorPrompt(String errorOutput)` que encola el mensaje con el template:
  ```
  El siguiente comando falló en el servidor. Analiza el error y propón una solución:

  <error output>
  ```
- La cola se drena en `initState` y cuando el widget vuelve a montarse, evitando race conditions si el usuario ya estaba escribiendo.

### `lib/view/pages/ServerPage.dart`
- Instancia `TerminalCommandTracker` y lo pasa tanto a `TerminalTab` como a `ChatIaTab`.
- El callback del botón "Preguntar a Pro-Tocol" llama a `chatController.injectErrorPrompt()` y navega al tab Chat IA.
- Se conecta al stdout del `SSHSession` pasando cada chunk por `tracker.filterStdoutForDisplay()` antes de escribirlo en xterm.

***

## 🏗️ Decisiones de Arquitectura

| Decisión | Alternativa descartada | Razón |
|---|---|---|
| Sentinel `echo "__PROTO_EXIT__:$?"` en stream SSH | `SSHSession.exitCode` future | `.exitCode` solo resuelve cuando el **canal** cierra, no entre comandos de un shell interactivo. El sentinel detecta exit code por comando individual. |
| Captura en capa SSH (antes de xterm) | Leer buffer interno de xterm | xterm no expone su buffer de texto. El único punto de lectura confiable es el `Stream<Uint8List>` del `SSHSession`. |
| `ChatIaController` con cola | Llamada directa a `IAService` | Si el usuario ya está escribiendo cuando se detecta el error, una llamada directa crearía una condición de carrera. La cola garantiza orden de ejecución. |
| `filterStdoutForDisplay()` antes de escribir a xterm | Filtrar en el tracker interno | Separar la responsabilidad de filtrado de la de captura hace que ambas sean testeables independientemente. |

***

## 🧪 Cómo Probar

1. Conectarse a un servidor.
2. En el tab **Terminal**, ejecutar un comando que falle (ej: `cat /archivo/que/no/existe`).
3. Verificar que aparece el banner **"Preguntar a Pro-Tocol"** en la parte inferior del terminal.
4. Verificar que la línea `__PROTO_EXIT__:1` **no** es visible en el terminal.
5. Tocar el botón → la app debe navegar al tab **Chat IA** con un mensaje de la IA analizando el error.
6. Ejecutar un comando exitoso → el banner debe desaparecer.

***

## 📎 Referencias

- Issue: `ES-49` (parent: `ES-44`)
- Branch: `ES-49-Explicador-Errores` → `develop`
- Archivos modificados: 4 (1 nuevo)
- Warnings resueltos: 0 (entregado en green)

body:
## Why the lambdas stopped working

Yahoo Finance started returning `HTTP 429 Too Many Requests` for the default User-Agent shipped by `yahoo-finance2` v2.x (the `@gadicc/` scope in the UA was being rejected by Yahoo). Reproed locally on `v2.13.3`:

- `chart` → `Unexpected token 'T', "Too Many Requests\r\n" is not valid JSON`
- `fundamentalsTimeSeries` → same
- `/v1/finance/search` (raw axios news call) → still works for now, but is subject to the same UA/crumb regime

Upstream fix: gadicc/yahoo-finance2#977, released in **v3.11.1** (latest is **v3.14.0**).

## What changed

- Bumped `yahoo-finance2` to `^3.14.0`.
- v3 is class-based, so we instantiate a singleton `new YahooFinance()` at module scope. Lambda warm invocations now reuse the cookie/crumb, which avoids re-doing the consent dance on every request.
- Replaced the raw `axios` call to `/v1/finance/search` with `yahooFinance.search()` so news goes through the same crumb-aware client. Dropped the `axios` dependency entirely.
- Handled the new `providerPublishTime` shape (`Date` in v3, used to be unix-seconds).
- Wrapped `handler` in a top-level `try/catch` so a transient Yahoo blip returns a clean JSON 5xx instead of bubbling up as a raw 5xx from API Gateway / Function URL.
- Factored out small `jsonResponse` / `errorResponse` / `requireParams` helpers to cut the duplication in the original file.

## Tested

Simulated Lambda events locally against the real Yahoo API:

```
[OPTIONS preflight]    status=200
[no action]            status=400  {"error":"Invalid action..."}
[prices missing]       status=400  {"error":"Missing start query param"}
[prices OK]            status=200  meta.symbol=AAPL, 10 quotes
[fundamentals OK]      status=200  quarterlyResult + annualResult populated
[news OK]              status=200  20 news items, ISO dates
[bad origin]           status=200  CORS falls back to localhost:5173 allowlist entry
```

## Deploy

No code changes needed in `/client`. Just re-zip and re-deploy:

```
cd server && ./README.sh   # ./zip.sh && cd .. && ./update-lambda.sh
```

## Summary

Production was returning 500 on every `/rest/v1/memberships?select=role,tenant:tenants(...)` call with Postgres error `42P17 — infinite recursion detected in policy for relation memberships`.

**Root cause:** the `memberships owner-write` policy on `public.memberships` (introduced in `supabase/migrations/20260430180000_tenant_rls_and_webhook_events.sql`) used a direct subquery against `public.memberships` inside a `FOR ALL` policy on that same table. RLS is re-evaluated on the inner SELECT, so the check recurses indefinitely.

**Fix:** add a new migration that

- introduces a `SECURITY DEFINER` helper `public.is_tenant_owner_or_admin(p_tenant_id UUID)` (same pattern as the existing `public.is_tenant_member`), so the membership lookup runs with definer rights and bypasses RLS;
- drops and recreates the `memberships owner-write` policy to call the helper instead of self-referencing `memberships`.

No behavior change beyond fixing the recursion — the policy still grants `FOR ALL` to owners and admins of the same tenant.

## Test plan

- [ ] Apply migration `20260516400000_fix_memberships_rls_recursion.sql` to a Supabase branch.
- [ ] As an authenticated tenant member, hit `/rest/v1/memberships?select=role,tenant:tenants(*)` and confirm it returns 200 instead of 500.
- [ ] As a tenant owner/admin, perform INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on `public.memberships` for a tenant they own — should succeed.
- [ ] As a non-owner/admin tenant member, the same writes should be denied.
- [ ] Confirm no other RLS policies regressed (`tenants member-read`, `memberships self-or-tenant`, etc.).
