author: carlheinmostert
body: ## Summary PDF export on `staging.session.homefit.studio` (and other cloud surfaces) sat forever on **"Rendering page 1 of 2…"** because PR #325's preload pipeline had no timeout and no `onclone` backstop, so a stalled Supabase signed-URL response (or a leftover unmapped ``) left `html2canvas`'s internal image loader hanging indefinitely. Embedded preview was unaffected because `homefit-local://` is same-origin. Applies the canonical fix pattern from the gotcha memory `gotcha_html2canvas_cors_taint.md`: - **Pre-fetch with timeout** — 8s `AbortController` budget per preload fetch. Stalled responses now surface as preload errors instead of hanging the pipeline. - **`onclone` backstop swap** — inside each per-page `html2canvas` call, re-walks the cloned DOM and swaps any unmapped `` src to its data URL. Imgs with no map entry get their src stripped, so `useCORS:true` never re-fetches a leftover Supabase URL (which would re-introduce the hang). - **`imageTimeout: 4000`** on html2canvas options + **15s `Promise.race` ceiling** on the whole per-page rasterise call. Belt-and-braces against any residual internal hang inside the library. - **Per-page `img.decode()` race guard** — wraps each cloned-page `decode()` in a 2s `setTimeout` race, matching the existing initial-decode pattern in `triggerLobbyShare` (line 2944+). Without this, a stuck decode on a broken data URL would freeze the pipeline at a specific page. - **Early-fail check** — when `dataUrlMap.size === 0 && preloadErrors.length > 0`, route to the existing "Couldn't generate the PDF" error modal + Retry button instead of letting the pipeline drift into the page loop. Live-DOM swap + data URLs (the original PR #325 approach) is preserved — the `onclone` swap is purely a backstop, not a replacement. This avoids the broken-image flicker and blob-URL revoke race that PR #325 documented in the preload comments. ## Files - `web-player/lobby.js` — primary surface (lobby export pipeline). - `app/assets/web-player/lobby.js` — drift-synced mirror for embedded preview. - `docs/test-scripts/pdf-tainted-canvas-fix.html` — 5-case verification script (cloud desktop, Mobile Safari, embedded preview, multi-page, failure path). ## Stacks on - PR #325 (multi-page PDF pipeline pivot from PNG) — the pre-fetch + swap mechanism already existed; this hotfix bounds its failure modes. - Gotcha memory: `gotcha_html2canvas_cors_taint.md` (PRs #265–#270 history, 5-round CORS-taint discovery). ## Test plan - [ ] Open a published plan on `staging.session.homefit.studio` (desktop browser) → tap Share → PDF generates without hang, modal swaps to preview thumbnail + Download/Share buttons. - [ ] Same on Mobile Safari — Web Share API opens iOS share sheet with the PDF attached. - [ ] Same on embedded preview (Flutter workflow Preview tab) — no regression, share sheet auto-fires after 250ms. - [ ] Plan with 8+ exercises (multi-page) — "Rendering page N of M…" progression visible, all pages render, page count badge correct. - [ ] Failure path — DevTools block one Supabase URL, then ALL Supabase URLs. Modal switches to "Couldn't generate the PDF: every image preload failed…" + Retry button (no infinite spinner). - [ ] CI: `web-player-drift-guard` passes (lockstep edit), Flutter checks green. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

- Add migration `netlify/database/migrations/0019_magic_link_profile_columns.sql` to ensure optional `client_name`/`client_phone` columns exist on legacy installs.

### Motivation
- Provide a formal, detailed integration contract between cjprestamos and HogarIA based on a deep analysis of the HogarIA repository and its existing external-loans module. 
- Clarify operational expectations (read-only vs sync), payload schemas, idempotency, security gaps and non-functional requirements to reduce risks during integration. 
- Offer a concrete roadmap and test matrix to guide safe rollout of the optional sync phase and future evolution (versioning, S2S auth, observability).

### Description
- Add a new documentation file `CONTRATO_INTEGRACION_HOGARIA.md` at the repository root that documents purpose, architecture summary, bounded contexts, remote endpoints, expected payload schemas, sync semantics, idempotency rules, security considerations, versioning policy, and recommended tests and roadmap. 
- The document enumerates the remote endpoints HogarIA consumes (`/loans/active`, `/dashboard`, `/control-caja`, `/loans/{id}/installments`, `/loans/{id}/payments`) and the expected fields, including the critical split `principalRecovered` / `interestCollected`. 
- It defines the three event types HogarIA creates for sync (`DISBURSEMENT`, `PAYMENT_PRINCIPAL_RECOVERY`, `PAYMENT_INTEREST_INCOME`) and prescribes idempotency and mapping rules to avoid duplicates. 
- This is a documentation-only change with no modifications to source code, migrations, or runtime configuration.

## Summary

Two commits on top of the post-PR-#30 audit:

### 1. `docs: refresh stale embed/CLI claims in README and design.md`

Fixes two outdated claims in user-facing docs.

**`README.md` — Deployment section.** The "**Note:** Embedding of
templates and static assets via `//go:embed` is designed but not yet
wired into the compiler" paragraph was stale. Embedding has been wired
for some time:

- `internal/compiler/compiler.go` emits `//go:embed templates/*` and
  `//go:embed static/*` directives into the generated `.gastro/embed.go`.
- `pkg/gastro/fs.go` (`GetTemplateFS` / `GetStaticFS`) switches between
  the embedded FS (prod) and the disk FS (dev, via `GASTRO_DEV=1`).
- `docs/design.md` §1 already lists Embedding as **Done**, and
  `docs/deployment.md` correctly describes the same wiring.

Rewrote the paragraph to describe what actually happens.

**`docs/design.md` §13 CLI.** The CLI table listed only
`generate` / `build` / `dev` and marked `gastro new` as *"Future: not
yet implemented"*. `gastro new` ships (`cmd/gastro/main.go:75`), as do
`watch`, `fmt`, `check`, `list`, `lsp`, and `version`. Replaced with
the full list shown by `gastro --help`.

### 2. `docs: add ROADMAP.md and link it from README`

New `ROADMAP.md` captures the deferred-work catalogue surfaced during
the post-PR-#30 audit. Twelve items, grouped by trigger:

- **Waiting on real adopter request** — six items across LSP, dev
  mode, and runtime / error handling (dict-key `Children` completion,

- **Larger roadmap items** — Go-native HTML completions in the LSP.

Each entry has a reference to the file or `DECISIONS.md` entry that
established the deferral. Items that are out of scope **by design**
(no Windows for `gastro watch`, no third-party runner dependency,
dot-imported `gastro.WithRequestFuncs` not detected by LSP, etc.) are
deliberately NOT on the roadmap — those point at the relevant
`DECISIONS.md` non-decisions sections.

README gains a one-line near-top pointer at ROADMAP.md plus
DECISIONS.md.

author: olemarkus
body:
## Summary

Symmetrize the midnight price-slot rotation between the Flow and Homey paths so the Homey path no longer drops its price horizon when the local date rolls over.

**Bug:** `getCombinedHourlyPricesFromHomey` called `purgeStaleFlowPriceSlots` with `allowTomorrowAsToday: false`. At local midnight the stored "tomorrow" payload is now dated today, but the Homey path cleared both the today and tomorrow slots instead of promoting tomorrow into today the way the Flow path does. Until the next periodic refresh fetched fresh data, `getCombinedHourlyPrices` returned an empty list and the daily-budget shaper fell back to uniform with `reasonCode: objective_missing_price_horizon`.

**Fix:** Both paths now share the same promotion behavior. The `allowTomorrowAsToday` parameter is removed from `purgeStaleFlowPriceSlots` and `buildCombinedHourlyPricesFromPayloads` since both call sites needed `true`. A new regression test (`test/homeyPriceService.test.ts`) exercises the Homey path end-to-end through `service.getCombinedHourlyPrices()`, mirroring the existing Flow promotion test.

body:
# Support Podman (and other OCI runtimes) in CDK publishing steps

<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

## Description

<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->

Read `ASPIRE_CONTAINER_RUNTIME` from the environment (defaulting to `docker`) wherever the CDK publish pipeline previously hardcoded the `docker` binary:

- `DefaultTarballContainerImageBuilder`: uses the runtime when building the `save` command
- `CDKPublishingStep.FixCDKAssetsFileForWindows`: uses the runtime when building the PowerShell `load` command

## Motivation and Context

<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
<!--- If it fixes an open issue, please link to the issue here -->

Users running Podman instead of Docker could not publish without symlinking `podman` to `docker`, because both publish paths hardcoded the `docker` binary name. The workaround is unsupported and breaks in environments where both runtimes coexist or where the user cannot write to system directories.

`ASPIRE_CONTAINER_RUNTIME` is already used by the core Aspire CLI to select between Docker and Podman for local run scenarios. Using the same variable keeps behaviour consistent across the Aspire ecosystem and requires no new user-facing API.

Usage with Podman:

```bash
ASPIRE_CONTAINER_RUNTIME=podman aspire publish -o ./publish
```

When the env var is unset the behaviour is identical to before (`docker`).

## Testing

<!--- Please describe in detail how you tested your changes -->
<!--- Include details of your testing environment, and the tests you ran to -->
<!--- see how your change affects other areas of the code, etc. -->

- Verified the project builds without errors or warnings
- Manually tested `aspire publish` with `ASPIRE_CONTAINER_RUNTIME=podman` on macOS with Podman installed
- Manually tested `aspire publish` without the env var set to confirm the default `docker` path is unchanged

## Breaking Changes Assessment

No breaking changes. When `ASPIRE_CONTAINER_RUNTIME` is unset the pipeline behaves exactly as before.

## Summary

S5-b ACT: ships three components on top of [PR #18975 (S5-a)](https://github.com/rjwalters/lean-genius/pull/18975)'s `shearM` / `shearM_lowerTriangular` / `shearM_det = (-1)^n` foundation:

- **`shearM_toLin'_apply_zero`** (~7 LOC) — `(shearM n α).toLin' v 0 = v 0`. Closed via `Finset.sum_eq_single 0` + shearM entry collapse (`Fin.cases_zero` → `1`; off-diagonal rows have outer-if false because `j ≠ 0`).
- **`shearM_toLin'_apply_succ`** (~12 LOC) — `(shearM n α).toLin' v i.succ = α i · v 0 − v i.succ`. Concise template from [S5 PREP-2 §5.1](https://github.com/rjwalters/lean-genius/pull/18622): `Fin.sum_univ_succ` peels j=0 (column 0 hit gives `α i` via `Fin.cases_succ`), then `Finset.sum_eq_single i` picks out the diagonal `j = i.succ` term (`-1`).
- **`dirichletBoxN`** def + **`dirichletSetN_eq_shearM_preimage`** (~30 LOC) — preimage identity `dirichletSetN n α Q = (shearM n α).toLin' ⁻¹' dirichletBoxN n Q`. The box is `Set.pi Set.univ` over `Fin (n+1)` with `(−(Qⁿ+1), Qⁿ+1)` on coordinate 0 and `(−1/Q, 1/Q)` on each `k.succ`, using `Fin.cases` to dispatch the bounds.

The preimage identity is the geometric bridge for S5-c: combined with `shearM_det = (-1)^n` (so `|det| = 1`) and `Real.map_matrix_volume_pi_eq_smul_volume_pi` ([S5 PREP-2 §6](https://github.com/rjwalters/lean-genius/pull/18622)), the box's product-measure volume `2(Qⁿ+1) · (2/Q)ⁿ = 2^(n+1)(Qⁿ+1)/Qⁿ` propagates back to `dirichletSetN`.

Total net change: lineCount 252 → 331 (+79), theoremCount 4 → 7 (+3), defCount 2 → 3 (+1), sorries 0 / axioms 0 unchanged.

## Build status

`./proofs/scripts/docker-build.sh Proofs.MinkowskiTheoremOQ02OQ03` (from worktree CWD) **→ 3058 jobs clean** (warm Mathlib cache, ~5 min wall). First attempt failed on `shearM_toLin'_apply_succ` (`simp only [Fin.cases_zero]` was unused, and the `Finset.sum_eq_single` residual `(if True then α i else 0)` wasn't reduced by `if_true`); second attempt swapped to `simp [Fin.succ_ne_zero]; ring` (and `simp [Fin.succ_ne_zero, hsuccne]` for the j ≠ i branch) and passed.

Log: `.loom/logs/researcher-9-minkowski-s5b-build2.log`.

**Lean-only**. Does not touch `state.md` / `research JSON` (avoids conflict with the open Session 8 STATE-SYNC [PR #18991](https://github.com/rjwalters/lean-genius/pull/18991), which will be touched up to reflect this S5-b after merge).

## Next ACT

**S5-c** (~80 LOC, the volume calculation itself): chain `dirichletSetN_eq_shearM_preimage` + `Real.map_matrix_volume_pi_eq_smul_volume_pi` (with `hdet_ne` from `shearM_det = (-1)^n`) + `volume_pi_Ioo` to compute `volume (dirichletSetN n α Q) = ENNReal.ofReal (2^(n+1) · (Qⁿ+1) / Qⁿ)`. The four Mathlib bearers are all verified at the pinned rev (S5 PREP-2 §1–§6).

## Summary
- repair the malformed `mcp/appwrite/package.json` and commit a valid `package-lock.json`
- remove the duplicated scaffold blocks that were pasted into `server.ts`, `tooling.ts`, and the tool modules
- replace the blocked runtime/toolchain dependencies with a self-contained Node 22+ scaffold that now installs, validates, builds, and runs locally in this environment
- add a dedicated Appwrite Function entrypoint so the package can reuse the same MCP runtime in Appwrite-managed execution as well as local server mode

## Root Cause
The merged scaffold combined multiple generations of the package files into the same sources. `package.json` ended up malformed, several TypeScript files contained duplicate pasted implementations, and the package still depended on external npm modules that were not installable in the current execution environment.

## What Changed
- cleaned `mcp/appwrite/package.json` into a valid manifest with native validation/build scripts
- added `mcp/appwrite/package-lock.json`

author: performance308
body:
Wave 2 Step 4 — when users navigate to a dashboard from a service context, pre-bind variables only after explicit first-open confirmation. Same variable set → no re-prompt. Different set → re-prompt.

## Why it matters

Per Open Risks in the design doc: wrong namespace = wrong data. Silent variable injection is the high-stakes path that breaks trust. This PR enforces first-open ack.

## Changes

### Backend
- New table \`dashboard_variable_ack\` (sqlite + postgres) — \`UNIQUE(user_id, dashboard_uid, vars_hash)\`
- \`IDashboardVariableAckRepository\` + sqlite/postgres/InMemory impls per ADR-001
- Shared hash util \`packages/common/src/utils/variable-hash.ts\` (FNV-1a 8-char hex, web-bundle safe — no node:crypto)
- REST:
  - \`GET /api/dashboards/:uid/variable-ack?vars=<hash>\` → \`{ acked: boolean }\`
  - \`POST /api/dashboards/:uid/variable-ack\` body \`{ vars: Record<string,string> }\` → server-hashes, upserts

### Frontend
- Hook \`useInferredVariables(dashboardUid)\` — reads \`?_inf_<key>=<value>\` URL params, hashes, checks ack
- \`VariableInferenceBanner\` component — [Use these] / [Change variables] / [Don't auto-bind]
- Wired into \`DashboardWorkspace.tsx\` above \`VariableBar\`. Only the \`applied\` state injects values; un-acked vars never reach query execution.

### Edge cases decided
- Empty-string values dropped from canonical form
- Duplicate \`_inf_<key>\` params: first wins (URLSearchParams.get behavior)
- Non-string POST body values → 400
- Fetch failure on GET ack → fall back to "needs ack" (show banner) — prefer to ask than silently bind

## Test plan

- [x] 19/19 tests pass (7 hash unit, 6 repo unit, 6 REST integration)
- [x] Order-invariance, value-sensitivity, hash discrimination assertions
- [x] First-open → POST → banner gone → reopen with same hash → no banner
- [x] Hash change reproduces banner
- [ ] CI green

## Wave 2.2 wiring

Services page (not yet merged) is where \`?_inf_service=...&_inf_namespace=...\` URLs will originate. Hook is unconditional — activates as soon as Wave 2.2 lands.

author: vaderyang
body:
## Summary

opencode (https://opencode.ai) is a Bun/TS CLI that talks OpenAI Chat Completions. Recent releases (≥ 1.14.x) attach a stable session id to every request:

\`\`\`
User-Agent: opencode/1.14.50 ai-sdk/provider-utils/4.0.23 runtime/bun/1.3.13
x-session-affinity: ses_1d9b5b09affe2vyaYUaMI4M5aS
\`\`\`

Without a dedicated profile, opencode falls through to GenericProfile, which derives session_id from \`text_hash(first_user_text + first_assistant_sig)\`. That hash is **not stable across user turns of the same chat** because the conversation prefix grows — so a long opencode chat splinters into multiple \`gen-*\` session ids, and the UI shows each user turn as its own detached 1-call AgentTurn instead of one multi-turn session.

## Approach

Add \`OpencodeProfile\` mirroring \`ClaudeCliProfile\` / \`CodexCliProfile\`:

| Field | Source |
|---|---|
| name | \`"opencode"\` |
| wire_api gate | \`OPENAI_CHAT\` |
| match | UA starts with \`opencode/\` AND header \`x-session-affinity\` present |
| session_id | the affinity header value, verbatim |
| extract_user_input / is_user_turn_start / extract_assistant_text | delegate to \`wa::openai::chat\` helpers |
| is_turn_terminal | trait default (opencode's \`finish_reason\` channel is reliable) |

Registered after \`codex-cli\` and **before** the body-fingerprint profiles (\`openclaw\`, \`hermes\`) so the cheap header check runs first.

### Failure-mode policy

Pre-1.14.x opencode lacks the affinity header — the profile **deliberately does not match** those calls (they'd produce \`extract_session_id = None\` with no fallback). They continue to fall through to GenericProfile, same as before.

## Verification

* \`cargo test -p ts-llm\` — 354 pass (includes new OpencodeProfile suite + two priority tests)
* New tests cover:
  * UA + header → matches (case-insensitive)
  * UA only (no affinity header) → does NOT match
  * Different wire api / different UA → does NOT match
  * Two calls with **growing message history** but the same affinity header produce the **same** session id (the regression that motivated the work)
* Build green on wuneng + binary hot-deployed; awaiting next live opencode call to confirm \`agent_kind=opencode\` appears in the dropdown (which auto-populates from the agent-kinds filter PR #16).

## Test plan

- [ ] Hit opencode → wait for one new chat round-trip
- [ ] \`/agent-turns?preset=15m\`: latest opencode call shows \`agent_kind = opencode\` (new badge colour from PR #15)
- [ ] Filter dropdown auto-includes \`opencode\` (PR #16 covers this)
- [ ] Across multiple user turns of the same opencode session: all turns share one \`ses_*\` session id; session detail panel groups them into one AgentSession

## Summary

- **Fix duplicate wallet root cause**: `_run_checks = interaction_check` alias was missing on `_WorkView`, `_ShopView`, `XpConfigView`, and `CogManagerView`. On the deployed discord.py build, the missing alias silently bypasses auth checks — any user could trigger another user's work/shop dropdown, running the callback with the wrong `user_id` and hitting a different (empty) wallet.
- **Pin uid/gid to command context**: `_JobSelect` and `_ShopSelect` callbacks now use `self._ctx.author.id` / `self._ctx.guild.id` instead of `interaction.user.id` / `interaction.guild.id`, so coin operations always target the command invoker regardless of who fires the component.
- **Persistent storage auto-detection**: `db.py` now checks for a `/data/` directory (Railway/Render standard persistent volume mount) before falling back to `disbot/data/`. Logs a warning when a fresh database is created so data-loss deploys are immediately visible. `data_manager.py` gets the same detection and now respects `BOT_DB_PATH`.
- **Add `!balance` / `!bal` / `!wallet`**: Quick authoritative coin balance command to avoid confusion from stale embed history in the channel.
- **Fix `_run_checks` on `_ChannelCreatorView`**: Resolves the `AttributeError` that caused `!ccreate` to fail.

author: planeshifter
body:
Follow-up fixes for commits merged to `develop` between 2026-05-13 20:52 PDT (`360877d`) and 2026-05-14 02:11 PDT (`80b1ef7`).

## Description

Audit of the 15 first-parent commits merged to `develop` over the last 24 hours surfaced two high-signal items, grouped by package below. Each commit on this branch corresponds to a single package fix.

### `blas/ext/base/cindex-of-column`

-   Fixes incorrect JSDoc and TypeScript return descriptions introduced in `995d771` — `lib/cindex_of_column.js`, `lib/ndarray.js`, and `docs/types/index.d.ts` all said "unable to find a search vector" instead of "unable to find a matching column", contradicting both the README and the analogous `dindex-of-column` package.

### `blas/ext/base/zindex-of-column`

-   Fixes the copy-paste error introduced in `62dad13` where `lib/zindex_of_column.js`, `lib/ndarray.js`, and `docs/types/index.d.ts` described the no-match condition as "unable to find a search vector" rather than "matching column", replacing all 5 occurrences to match the README and `dindex-of-column` reference implementation.

## Related Issues

None.

## Questions

None.

## Other

### Validation

Audited the 15-commit window with two parallel style-compliance reviewers (compared each substantive new file against established reference packages — `dindex-of-column`/`sindex-of-column` for the new column-search packages, `transpose-operation-{str2enum,enum2str}` for the kmeans enum utilities, `ndarray/zeros`/`ndarray/ones` for `ndarray/nans`) and two parallel bug reviewers (one diff-only, one with full source-file context). Findings were de-duplicated and each surviving issue re-verified against the diff before applying.

Items raised during the audit but deliberately excluded from this PR:

-   Native C `_ndarray` routines in `cindex-of-column`/`zindex-of-column` use signed `strideA1 <= strideA2` for column-major detection while the JS path uses absolute-value `isColumnMajor`. The same divergence exists in the pre-existing `dindex-of-column`/`sindex-of-column`/`gindex-of-column` C sources, so addressing it would require a family-wide fix outside this window's scope.
-   "stride length for the first dimension" vs. "stride of the first dimension" wording in the new packages' JSDoc — the existing family is itself inconsistent (`sindex-of-column` uses "stride length for", `dindex-of-column` uses "stride of"); not a clear violation.
-   Re-adding the `numpy.nans` keyword to `ndarray/nans/package.json` — its removal in `65cbb12` is the explicit purpose of that commit.
-   Adding an `extended` keyword to the new `cindex-of-column`/`zindex-of-column` `package.json` files — the analogous `dindex-of-column` does not carry it, so no divergence exists.
-   `dnrm2` `@returns L2-norm` tag in `blas/base/ndarray/docs/types/index.d.ts` — matches the wording already used by the standalone `blas/base/dnrm2` and `blas/base/ndarray/dnrm2` declarations.

### Update

Originally this PR also proposed replacing the imported `isNumber`/`isString` guards in `ml/base/kmeans/algorithm-str2enum` and `algorithm-enum2str` with inline `typeof` checks to match the BLAS `*2enum` packages. Per review by @kgryte, the kmeans packages are correct as-is — it is the BLAS packages that should adopt the imported utility. Both commits have been dropped.

author: morganmcg1
body:
## Hypothesis

The current K=8 Caruana greedy ensemble uses weights constrained to integer multiples of 1/8 (i.e., {0.125, 0.250, 0.375, 0.500, ...}). The true continuous optimum on the 4-simplex may differ from these quantized weights and yield a lower val_WSS — especially for the lower-weighted members (ghh0s4ne=0.125) where the discrete grid is coarse.

This experiment uses **SLSQP continuous optimization** (scipy.optimize.minimize, method='SLSQP') to find the exact optimal weights w ∈ Δ₃ (4-simplex, summing to 1) on the same 4-member pool that minimizes val_WSS, subject to:
- val_vol_p ≤ 3.643% (SOTA test_vol_p ceiling)
- val_SP ≤ 3.577% (SOTA test_SP ceiling)

**Expected outcome**: weights near {56bcqp3m:0.36, 29nohj67:0.26, a0yoxy85:0.25, ghh0s4ne:0.13}, val_WSS improvement vs K=8 Caruana val_WSS=6.5195%, and potentially improved test_WSS vs 6.3263%.

## Current Baseline

| Metric | K=8 Caruana (PR #1102) |
|--------|------------------------|
| val_abupt | 5.7452% |
| val_vol_p | 3.4360% |
| val_WSS | 6.5195% |
| val_SP | 3.7234% |
| test_abupt | 5.5196% |
| test_vol_p | 3.5397% |
| test_SP | 3.3529% |
| test_WSS | 6.3263% |
| test_tau_x | 5.6071% |
| test_tau_y | 6.8397% |
| test_tau_z | 8.2585% |

**K=8 greedy weights**: {56bcqp3m: 0.375, 29nohj67: 0.250, a0yoxy85: 0.250, ghh0s4ne: 0.125}

**Win gate (NEW ENSEMBLE SOTA)**: val_abupt < 5.7452% AND test_vol_p ≤ 3.643% AND test_WSS < 6.3263% (all must hold)

## 4-Member Pool

| W&B Run ID | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| `56bcqp3m` | Primary SOTA run (alphonse, string-sep, full schedule) |
| `29nohj67` | Second Caruana pick |
| `a0yoxy85` | Third Caruana pick |
| `ghh0s4ne` | Fourth Caruana pick (ghh0s4ne, weight=0.125 in K=8) |

## Instructions

This experiment does **NOT** require GPU training. It is a pure Python optimization over pre-computed model predictions.

### Step 1: Set up SLSQP optimizer

Write a Python script (or use `ensemble_eval.py` if it supports continuous weights) that:

1. Loads the val-set predictions from the 4 W&B runs: `56bcqp3m`, `29nohj67`, `a0yoxy85`, `ghh0s4ne`
2. Forms the prediction ensemble as: `pred = w[0]*pred_56bcqp3m + w[1]*pred_29nohj67 + w[2]*pred_a0yoxy85 + w[3]*pred_ghh0s4ne`
3. Defines the objective: **minimize val_WSS** (weighted sum MAPE on surface WSS fields)
4. Defines constraints:
   - `sum(w) == 1`
   - `w[i] >= 0` for all i (simplex constraint)
   - `val_vol_p(w) <= 0.03643` (≤ 3.643%)
   - `val_SP(w) <= 0.03577` (≤ 3.577%)
5. Uses `scipy.optimize.minimize(method='SLSQP', bounds=[(0,1)]*4, constraints=[...])`
6. Runs from **multiple starting points** (at least 5):
   - K=8 Caruana weights: [0.375, 0.250, 0.250, 0.125]
   - Uniform: [0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25]
   - WSS-focused: [0.40, 0.30, 0.20, 0.10]
   - ghh0s4ne-boosted: [0.35, 0.25, 0.25, 0.15]
   - vol_p-relaxed: [0.45, 0.25, 0.20, 0.10]

### Step 2: Evaluate optimal weights

With the optimal w* found by SLSQP:

```bash
python ensemble_eval.py \
  --data-root /mnt/new-pvc/Processed/drivaerml_processed_rawcanon_20260511 \
  --wandb-run-ids 56bcqp3m 29nohj67 a0yoxy85 ghh0s4ne \
  --weights <w0> <w1> <w2> <w3> \
  --split val \
  --output-metrics val_metrics_slsqp.json

python ensemble_eval.py \
  --data-root /mnt/new-pvc/Processed/drivaerml_processed_rawcanon_20260511 \
  --wandb-run-ids 56bcqp3m 29nohj67 a0yoxy85 ghh0s4ne \
  --weights <w0> <w1> <w2> <w3> \
  --split test \
  --output-metrics test_metrics_slsqp.json
```

Also try the K=8 Caruana weights as a control to confirm your eval reproduces the baseline.

### Step 3: Also try unconstrained val_WSS minimization

Run a second SLSQP pass that **only** minimizes val_WSS with simplex constraints (no vol_p / SP ceiling). Report those weights and metrics too — this is the absolute floor on val_WSS achievable from this pool.

### Step 4: Report all results

Post a comment with:
- Optimal SLSQP weights (constrained and unconstrained)
- Objective function value at each starting point (confirm global optimum)
- Val metrics: val_abupt, val_vol_p, val_WSS, val_SP, val_tau_x/y/z
- Test metrics: test_abupt, test_vol_p, test_WSS, test_SP, test_tau_x/y/z
- Comparison table vs K=8 Caruana baseline

Terminal result marker (once you have final metrics):
```
SENPAI-RESULT: {"terminal":true,"status":"complete","pending_arms":false,"wandb_run_ids":["slsqp-no-training"],"primary_metric":{"name":"val_abupt","value":<value>},"test_metric":{"name":"test_WSS","value":<value>}}
```

## Notes

- No GPU needed for this experiment — it's pure Python optimization over cached predictions
- If `ensemble_eval.py` doesn't support continuous weights, write a thin wrapper that calls the metric computation function directly
- The val-set predictions may be cached on disk from prior ensemble runs; check `/mnt/new-pvc/` for any cached prediction files before re-running inference
- Report the SLSQP convergence info (fun value, success flag, number of iterations) for each starting point
- **Do not train any new models** — this is purely a post-hoc ensemble weight search

## Reproduce Command

```bash
python slsqp_ensemble_search.py \
  --data-root /mnt/new-pvc/Processed/drivaerml_processed_rawcanon_20260511 \
  --run-ids 56bcqp3m 29nohj67 a0yoxy85 ghh0s4ne \
  --objective val_WSS \
  --constraints "val_vol_p<=0.03643,val_SP<=0.03577" \
  --n-starts 5 \
  --wandb-group edward-slsqp-ensemble
```

jobs:
  unittest:
    name: unittest (${{ matrix.os }}, ${{ matrix.python-version }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest]

author: ansocode
body:
## Summary

- Route central-side aggregators in `/api/fleet/*` and `/api/nodes/:id/meta` through `NodeRegistry.getProxyTarget` so the loopback URL backed by the active pilot tunnel is used uniformly. Pilot-agent rows now populate capabilities, version, CPU/RAM/Disk, stacks list, stack-drilldown, and per-node dashboard configuration instead of returning nulls.
- Filter pilot-side capabilities at boot to exclude features whose central-to-pilot path is not yet wired (`host-console`, `self-update`). Keeps the Console tab from rendering on pilot-active sessions and silently routing to central's host through the WS upgrade gate that still keys on `api_url + api_token`.
- Drop the cached `/api/meta` response on tunnel reconnect so the next request rebuilds capabilities and version through the live bridge instead of waiting for the 3-minute TTL.
- Repair the Husky `commit-msg` hook (add missing shebang + `.gitattributes` rule pinning `.husky/*` to LF) so commits do not fail with "Exec format error" on Windows shells where autocrlf converts the hook to CRLF.

## Test plan

- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean for backend and frontend
- [x] Three new test files green (19 tests): `capability-registry-pilot`, `node-registry-fetch-meta`, `fleet-pilot-agent-parity` cover the Authorization-header behavior, pilot-mode filter idempotency, `fetchMetaForNode` dispatch (offline target, pilot-agent loopback, proxy-mode), and the four affected fleet routes for pilot-agent both when the tunnel is up and when it is down.
- [x] Existing `fleet`, `pilot-agent-proxy`, and `mesh-list-stacks-remote` suites still green.
- [ ] Production verification: switch the active node on a fleet that contains a real pilot-agent (e.g. sencho-pilot-test), confirm the Fleet card renders real CPU/RAM/Disk and the version badge stops saying "Update available". Click into a stack on the card to verify the drilldown returns containers without a 503. Stop the pilot container, confirm the card flips to offline gracefully and recovers within seconds after restart (cache invalidates on tunnel-up).

## Notes

- The four self-update paths in `routes/fleet.ts` (`/fleet/nodes/:id/update`, `/fleet/update-all`) intentionally remain gated on `node.api_url && node.api_token`. Pilot-agent self-update is out of scope; pilots ship as a managed Docker container and rely on the central operator for image bumps.
- The pilot-side capability filter (`applyPilotModeCapabilityFilter`) is the data-source fix for the Console-tab hazard. A future PR can plumb the WS upgrade through the loopback bridge and re-enable the capability.
- The `noTargetMessage` helper produces a mode-aware 503 (`Pilot tunnel to "name" is disconnected.` vs `Remote node not configured`) so the drilldown surfaces the right diagnostic instead of the proxy-mode "configure API URL" copy.

author: quendo05
body:
This pull request introduces several improvements and new features to both the backend and frontend of the MiniJiraAspire project, focusing on enhanced filtering, error handling, and data consistency. The main changes include support for filtering tasks and epics by project, improved error and loading states in the UI, and better handling of task-epic relationships.

**Backend Enhancements:**

*Task and Epic Filtering:*
- Added `projectId` as an optional filter for tasks and epics, updating endpoints, queries, and repository methods to support it
- Extended the epics API and query keys to accept filters, and updated type definitions for epics to include `projectId` (`epicApi.ts`, `epicTypes.ts`, `useEpicsQuery.ts`).

*Task-Epic Relationship Handling:*
- Modified the epic deletion logic to unassign all tasks from an epic before the epic is deleted, ensuring data consistency (`EpicRepository.cs`).
- Updated the assign-epic command to allow unassigning an epic from a task (by passing a `null` epicId), and adjusted the repository accordingly (`AssignEpicCommand.cs`).

**Frontend Improvements:**

*UI/UX and Error Handling:*
- Enhanced the `AssignTicketsModal`, `CreateEpicModal`, and `EpicBacklogCard` components to display loading and error states, and to provide retry options when fetching tickets fails. Also, added user-friendly messages and links for empty states (`AssignTicketsModal.tsx`, `CreateEpicModal.tsx`, `EpicBacklogCard.tsx`).
- Updated the modals and ticket rows to consistently use `displayId` for ticket identification instead of the internal `id`, improving clarity for users.
- Removed the static workspace state card from the main layout, cleaning up the UI (`AppLayout.tsx`).

*API and Data Consistency:*
- Added an API function for assigning and unassigning epics to tasks, supporting the new backend logic (`taskApi.ts`). 

These changes collectively improve the flexibility, reliability, and user experience of the application, especially in projects with multiple epics and tasks.

body:
_ShardIndex previously inferred the chunk grid shape from
offsets_and_lengths.shape[:-1]. For 0-D arrays this collapses the array
to rank-1, breaking methods that assume rank >= 2 and forcing a numpy
compat cast workaround.

Store chunks_per_shard as an explicit NamedTuple field instead. This
removes the chunks_per_shard property and its cast, and lets several
call sites use the field directly instead of reverse-engineering it.

Also removes the unused `_ShardIndex.is_dense` method (ported from an
earlier prototype, no call sites in the repo, no test coverage). Thanks
to @ilan-gold for catching it in review.

Closes #3974

author: hendrikgc02
body:
@
**Status:** real bug fixed. Per-channel CPU/GPU means now match within 4% (was 3× off). The numeric SSIM gate of ≥0.97 at 64 spp is not achievable with the current dual-RNG architecture; see "Test-gate observation" below.

## Root cause

The 3× green-channel bias was an **order-of-operations** asymmetry between CPU and GPU integration:

| | CPU (`raytracer.h:2548-2595`) | GPU before (`multiwavelength_kernel.cu`) |
|---|---|---|
| per sample | `sCol = finiteVecOrZero(XYZ)` → firefly-clamp on **XYZ.Y** > 20 → `color += sCol` (XYZ accumulate) | `xyz = spectrumToXYZ(rad)` → `sample = xyzToLinearSRGB(xyz)` (per-sample!) → firefly-clamp on **sRGB lum** > 20 → `colorRGB += sample` |
| after SPP | `color /= samples` → `xyzToLinearSRGB(color)` once | `colorRGB /= samples` |

`xyzToLinearSRGB` contains a non-linear "negative-channel lift" (`if (minC < 0) { r-=minC; g-=minC; b-=minC; }`) that does **not commute with averaging**. For the test HDRI with bluish samples, the row `r = 3.24·X − 1.54·Y − 0.50·Z` produces negative R on a large fraction of samples (high Z, low X). The per-sample lift adds `|R|` to G and B *every single sample*, baking the inflation into the average. CPU averages XYZ first and lifts exactly once after a single conversion.

## Fix

`src/gpu/multiwavelength_kernel.cu` — accumulate XYZ across SPP, convert to linear sRGB once at the end, firefly-clamp on XYZ.Y to match CPU.

Diff is +31/-8 in a single kernel.

## Measured impact

Probe scene = exact test HDRI (32×16, blue/red gradient + bright green firefly at value `(0, 50, 0)`), camera and integrator settings match `test_gpu_cpu_ssim_hdri`:

**Per-channel GPU/CPU means (lower is better, 1.000 = parity):**

|  | R | G | B |
|---|---|---|---|
| pre-fix (`fa636c5`) | 1.0 | **3.0** | 1.1 |
| post-fix (this PR) | 1.026 | **1.038** | 0.979 |

The 3× green bias is gone.

**SSIM trajectory at fix:**

| SPP | SSIM |
|---|---|
| 64 | 0.452 |
| 256 | 0.678 |
| 1024 | 0.868 |

Converges with √SPP as expected for an MC-noise-limited metric.

## Test-gate observation (owner decision needed)

The test asserts SSIM ≥ 0.97 at **64 spp**. The remaining gap at low SPP is **RNG noise**, not parity: CPU uses `std::mt19937`, GPU uses `curand`, and they sample the HDRIs bright green firefly at different pixels of the output. The fireflys post-clamp per-pixel contribution is ~20 (`XYZ.Y` clamp), while the gradient background is ~0.5 — thats a 40:1 luminance ratio whose discrete spatial placement dominates SSIM at sparse sampling.

To close 0.97 wed need one of:
1. Raise gate SPP to ~4096 (slow but principled).
2. Gaussian-pre-filter both images before SSIM (standard practice for noisy renders).
3. Replace the firefly in the test HDRI — its there for the rotation test (`test_rotation_changes_env_lookup`), not for this SSIM test.
4. Relax the gate (e.g. 0.85 at 256 spp).

Recommend (2) or (3); they preserve the tests intent. **Out of scope for this PR** — flagged for separate decision.

## Whats in this PR

- `src/gpu/multiwavelength_kernel.cu`: the order-of-ops fix.

Reverts the agents prior bilinear-spectral-tint rewrite? **No** — that change is also correct and stays. The remaining `fa636c5` work (route `path_tracer` to MW kernel, spectral tint via `GSPEC_RGB_ILLUMINANT` + bilinear in spectral space) is necessary; the order-of-ops fix is additive on top.

## Provenance (CLAUDE.md §6)

The CPU integration order (XYZ accumulate, convert once) is the conventional pattern in PBRT-v4 (`src/pbrt/cameras.cpp` `Film::AddSample` and tile finalize) and Cycles (`intern/cycles/integrator/path_trace_tile.cpp`). Im not citing a new algorithm — Im restoring parity with the existing CPU code that already follows it.

## Description

Bumped the build toolchain for the `reloader` binary (`/usr/bin/reloader`) inside the `vector` image of the `log-shipper` module from Go 1.24 to Go 1.25.

The `vector` binary itself is written in Rust and is not affected. Only the small Go-based `reloader` sidecar is rebuilt.

Changes:
- `modules/460-log-shipper/images/vector/werf.inc.yaml`: switched the `vector-reloader-artifact` `from:` to `builder/golang-alpine-1.25`.
- `modules/460-log-shipper/images/vector/reloader/go.mod`: bumped `go` version to `go1.25.8`.

## Why do we need it, and what problem does it solve?

Trivy reports CVEs against `usr/bin/reloader` in the `vector` image (module `log-shipper`).

## Why do we need it in the patch release (if we do)?

Required for the 1.73.x patch line. CVEs in the embedded Go stdlib are surfaced by security scanners on customer clusters and must be closed in the supported release branch.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Initial implementation of a Telegram sniper-style trading bot for the TON blockchain.

**Stack:** Python 3.11+, aiogram 3.x, tonutils 0.5.8 (STON.fi V2 helpers), aiosqlite, cryptography (Fernet), matplotlib, GeckoTerminal public API.

**Features**

- Multi-wallet support
  - Create new wallet (v3r2 / v4r2 / v5r1; default v5r1) — mnemonic shown once, encrypted at rest
  - Import wallet by mnemonic with version selector
  - List / switch / delete wallets; one wallet marked default per user
- Encryption at rest via Fernet (`WALLET_ENCRYPTION_KEY` env var, no fallback)
- Token info card — name / symbol / price / 24h change / FDV / liquidity / 24h volume, sourced from GeckoTerminal
- 1h OHLCV chart (matplotlib Agg backend → PNG attached to message)
- Buy flow: paste Jetton master → quick TON amount presets (0.1 / 0.5 / 1 / 5 / 10) or custom → simulate via STON.fi `/v1/swap/simulate` → confirm → broadcast via `tonutils` `StonfiRouterV2` helpers
- Sell flow: paste Jetton master → show wallet balance → 25 / 50 / 75 / 100 % presets or custom → simulate → confirm → broadcast
- Per-user slippage settings (presets 0.5 / 1 / 3 / 5 / 10 % or custom 0.01–50 %), stored in SQLite
- Limit orders
  - Create (side, jetton, amount, USD trigger, 30-day expiry, current slippage)
  - List & cancel
  - Background asyncio worker polls every 30 s, batches price lookups per jetton, executes triggered orders, notifies the user via Telegram, and expires stale orders
- Access control: `is_public` flag (default true) or `ALLOWED_USER_IDS` whitelist
- SQLite (aiosqlite) for persistence; schema covers `users`, `wallets`, `limit_orders` with proper foreign keys and CHECK constraints
- ruff lint clean; basic pytest smoke tests pass

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Change the default branch.** The repo was empty when I started; the integration token couldn't create `main` directly, so I pushed a placeholder `main` via the API and merged it into this feature branch. After merging, switch the default branch from `devin/1778761586-initial-scaffold` to `main` in repo Settings → Branches.
- [ ] **Set `WALLET_ENCRYPTION_KEY` securely.** It must be a base64-urlsafe 32-byte key (`python -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())"`). Losing it bricks every stored wallet. Mnemonics are encrypted with it — anyone with the key can sweep funds.
- [ ] **Run the bot once locally and verify mainnet flows with a small amount** before trusting it with real value. Suggested smoke run:
  1. `cp .env.example .env`, fill `BOT_TOKEN` / `WALLET_ENCRYPTION_KEY` / `TONCENTER_API_KEY`.
  2. `pip install -e .` then `python -m ton_sniper_bot`.
  3. `/start` → Create wallet → fund it with ~1 TON → Buy a low-cap Jetton with `0.1 TON` → wait for confirmation in https://tonviewer.com → Sell 25 %.
  4. Create a limit order with a trigger just below current price; verify it executes within ~30 s of crossing.
- [ ] **STON.fi router auto-discovery.** I always call `POST /v1/swap/simulate?dex_v2=true` to get the active router address dynamically — no hard-coded addresses. If STON.fi changes the response shape this would break; sanity check on the first trade.
- [ ] **Limit-order persistence.** Orders survive bot restart (stored in SQLite). The worker resumes them automatically. Verify by restarting between order creation and trigger.
- [ ] **Concurrency / re-entrancy.** A single user firing multiple limit orders on the same wallet can race because there's no per-wallet lock. For v0.1 the polling interval (30 s) makes this unlikely but not impossible.

### Notes

- **No testnet support** — `NETWORK=testnet` is allowed in config but the STON.fi API and tonutils helpers I wired up target mainnet. Switching to testnet would require swapping the router class and is intentionally out of scope.
- **Charts** fall back to a placeholder PNG when GeckoTerminal has no pool / OHLCV for a token. This is rare for tradable Jettons.
- **Mnemonic visibility** — mnemonic is displayed once in chat after wallet creation. aiogram doesn't expose self-deleting messages, so the user is told to delete the chat manually. Could be added later via a follow-up task that schedules a `delete_message` call.
- **DEX scope** — STON.fi V2 only. DeDust support was scoped out for v0.1.
- **Provided secrets** (BOT_TOKEN, TONCENTER_API_KEY, TONAPI_KEY) are stored as session-only environment variables in my sandbox; they are **not** committed to the repo. Save them via the Devin secrets UI if you want them persisted across future sessions.

### Architecture

```
src/ton_sniper_bot/
├── config.py            # Settings dataclass + .env loader
├── crypto_box.py        # Fernet wrapper
├── db.py                # aiosqlite schema + CRUD (users / wallets / limit_orders)
├── logging_setup.py
├── ton/
│   ├── client.py        # ToncenterV3Client factory
│   ├── wallets.py       # create / restore (v3r2 / v4r2 / v5r1)
│   └── jettons.py       # balance queries
├── dex/
│   ├── stonfi.py        # /v1/swap/simulate + StonfiRouterV2 swap-tx builders
│   └── service.py       # high-level preview_buy / preview_sell / execute_trade
├── market/
│   ├── gecko.py         # GeckoTerminal client with 30s cache
│   └── chart.py         # matplotlib candle PNG renderer
├── bot/
│   ├── main.py          # composes deps + starts long polling
│   ├── states.py        # FSM groups
│   ├── keyboards.py     # inline keyboards (RU)
│   ├── texts.py         # message templates / formatters
│   └── handlers/        # start, wallet, settings, buy, sell, limits
└── workers/
    └── limit_orders.py  # background poller (30s)
```

body:
## Summary

Project 21 residual cleanup for Host issues #264 and #275.

### #264 — Thread-scoped mailbox duplicate sparse rows

Root cause: thread-scoped mailbox reads query `gsi2` by thread partition only. Mailbox state-change event rows intentionally share the thread `gsi2PK` for audit/history, but their `gsi2SK` starts with `EVENT#`, so they could be hydrated through the message model as sparse duplicate same-delivery rows after read/unread/reply mutations.

Fix:

- constrain thread-scoped mailbox message queries to `gsi2SK BEGINS_WITH MSG#`
- add regression coverage asserting the thread query uses the message-row sort-key prefix

### #275 — Private mint-conversation generic route/access log hardening

Fix:

- add `observability.SanitizeLogPath` for private mint-conversation single-read paths:
  - Host instance route: `/api/v1/soul/instance/agents/{agentId}/mint-conversations/{conversationId}`
  - Lesser self-scope proxy-shaped path if it ever passes through Host logging: `/api/v1/souls/bound/me/mint-conversations/{conversationId}`
- hash-normalize the private `conversationId` segment and drop query/fragment suffixes on those private single-read paths so raw cursors/fragments are not persisted with the sanitized path
- apply path sanitization before Host generic AppTheory request logs, AppTheory metric `tags.path` logs, and derived EMF metric details
- change control-plane HTTP API access logs to persist `$context.routeKey` instead of raw `$context.path`
- add an explicit templated HTTP API route for the Host private single-read route so API Gateway access logs preserve route class without raw `conversationId`
- keep dedicated Host instance-read audit behavior unchanged: hashed actor/instance/agent/conversation identifiers only
- hash agent/conversation identifiers in mint-conversation update-failure log lines

Sibling scope:

- The Lesser self-scope proxy route is not Host-owned. I created equaltoai/lesser#955 and linked it from #275 rather than expanding Host scope silently.

## Validation

- `go test ./internal/observability`
- `go test ./internal/controlplane ./internal/observability`
- `go test ./...`
- `cd cdk && npm test`
- `bash gov-infra/verifiers/gov-verify-rubric.sh` → PASS 29 / FAIL 0 / BLOCKED 0

Notes: `cd cdk && npm test` still emits existing CloudFront `S3Origin` deprecation warnings and existing Lightning CSS `:global(...)` warnings from the web build; tests pass.

## Ops probe steps

- For #264: reproduce self-send → read/unread → reply → `email_read(threadId=...)`; expected result is one row per delivery, no same-delivery sparse duplicates with empty subject/body.
- For #275: call the Host instance route `/api/v1/soul/instance/agents/{agentId}/mint-conversations/{conversationId}` and verify:
  - Host generic Lambda request logs contain a sanitized path with `conversation-sha256:<16hex>` rather than the raw conversation ID
  - Host generic AppTheory metric logs contain sanitized `tags.path` with `conversation-sha256:<16hex>` rather than the raw conversation ID
  - control-plane HTTP API access logs use the templated route key, not raw `$context.path`
  - dedicated `soul_mint_instance_read` audit/access logs continue to show hashed identifiers only

Closes #264
Closes #275

author: copilot
body:
The README did not clearly explain how Kagami treats saved cursors, full reloads, scoped syncs, and persisted link state during matching and pruning. This update adds that missing behavior documentation and reframes the examples around contact/category filters rather than calendar events.

- **Sync semantics**
  - Adds a dedicated section describing how incremental runs use saved cursors and treat omitted items as implicitly unchanged.
  - Clarifies when Kagami falls back to a full load and that both cursors are replaced together when establishing a new baseline.

- **Scope and prune boundaries**
  - Documents that historical link rows only participate when one side is present in the current loaded sets.
  - Explains why scoped full loads are safe with `--prune`: contacts outside the current scope on both sides are inert for that run.

- **Matching and deletion rules**
  - Describes how persisted links are honored first, then unmatched in-scope contacts are paired via normal matching rules.
  - Clarifies that create/update/delete decisions only apply within the current comparison set.

- **Examples and invariant**
  - Replaces event-based examples with contact/category-filter examples.
  - Adds an explicit safety invariant summarizing the planner boundary.

Example added to illustrate scoped behavior:

```bash
kagami contacts sync \
  --from Microsoft \
  --to Google \
  --filter "contains(categories,'Recruiter')" \
  --prune \
  --settings appsettings.json
```

With that scope on both sides, contacts outside the `Recruiter` category do not participate in matching or prune decisions unless one of their linked IDs appears in the current loaded sets.

| [config/providers.yaml](config/providers.yaml) | tech: ~ → tech: wappalyzer_oss |
| [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml) | + python-Wappalyzer + setuptools<81 (pkg_resources hack — see notes) |
| [tests/test_wappalyzer_oss.py](tests/test_wappalyzer_oss.py) | 10 tests, library mocked at the sync helper boundary |

## Why this completes a meaningful arc

Four providers wired now across four different shapes:
- **HTTP (no auth)** — SEC EDGAR
- **HTTP (bearer)** — Firecrawl
- **HTTP (x-api-key)** — Exa
- **Local Python lib** — Wappalyzer OSS

That proves the Strategy pattern is general — any future provider (REST API, gRPC, subprocess, in-process library) can plug in via the same interface. From here it's mechanical to add the remaining ones (Apollo for /people, Google Trends for /traffic).

## How tested

- [x] \`ruff check .\` + \`ruff format --check .\` — clean
- [x] \`pytest -q\` — **131 passed** (122 prior + 10 new -1 from a renamed test). Note: 60s total because the timeout test legitimately waits.
- [ ] CI on this PR

## Trade-offs documented in the code

**Setuptools pin (\`<81\`):** python-Wappalyzer imports \`pkg_resources\`, which setuptools 81 removed. The pin is a known-temporary hack with a documented sunset path: swap to \`wappalyzer-next\` (Playwright-based, fresh fingerprints, ~200MB Chromium download for the container) when either pkg_resources is fully gone or the fingerprints get too stale.

**Cache TTL = 7d static:** tech stacks change rarely. Switching from React to Vue is a months-long migration; CDN swap is usually one-shot. 7-day cache is the right granularity.

## Risk & rollback

**Risk:** medium. The setuptools pin restricts the deps universe; future PRs adding a package that requires setuptools≥81 would conflict. Mitigation: documented in pyproject.toml comment + this PR description.

**Rollback:** \`git revert <merge-sha>\`. Removes /tech, sets \`tech: ~\` in providers.yaml so route would 503, removes the python-Wappalyzer + setuptools pin.

## Operational

- No API key required
- python-Wappalyzer ships fingerprint database in the package; no runtime download
- Cache means most lookups never hit upstream

## Security checklist

- [x] No secrets in code, commits, or logs (no API key for this provider)
- [x] HttpUrl on primary_url rejects javascript:/data:/file: at parse time
- [x] subprocess-style execution wrapped in asyncio.wait_for with 30s timeout — runaway can't block the event loop
- [x] _AnalyzeError wraps all library failures; route never sees raw library exceptions

author: akhilyad
body:
🎯 **What:** The `PythonExecTool` previously executed arbitrary user-provided code using `subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", code])` without any sandboxing or limitations, allowing arbitrary code execution (RCE).
⚠️ **Risk:** A malicious or misguided AI agent could execute arbitrary system commands (e.g., `os.system`), spawn subprocesses, read/write sensitive files directly via `open()`, make outbound network requests, and access memory objects, compromising the host system.
🛡️ **Solution:** Implemented a robust Python execution sandbox using `sys.addaudithook`. 
- Denies dangerous events directly in Python C-level hooks, including `os.system`, `subprocess.Popen`, `os.exec`, `socket.connect`, `open`, etc.
- Prevents importing of dangerous modules (`os`, `subprocess`, `ctypes`, `socket`, `pathlib`, `io`, etc).
- Clears pre-loaded system modules prior to `exec()` so that variables or traversals through `sys.modules` cannot bypass the auditing layer.
- Retains existing expected Python code execution functionality for safe data analysis/math tasks while removing access to the system.

author: dougborg
body:
## Summary

- Marks 6 OpenAPI spec fields nullable to match the live Katana wire (the spec was strictly tighter than reality) — fixes the `'NoneType' object is not iterable` / `has no len()` crashes that took down `get_variant_details`, `check_inventory`, and the cache warmup since at least 2026-05-11.
- Extends `regenerate_client.py`'s ty-cast patcher to handle the union-aware loop pattern that the OpenAPI generator emits when an array property is `[array, "null"]`.
- Adds `cache_warmup_partial` traceback capture so the next regression is one-shot diagnosable instead of silently swallowed.
- Pins the wire contract with `TestWireNullTolerance` in `tests/test_models_pydantic.py` — 8 cases covering each crash site.

Closes #727.

## Spec changes (with rationale)

| Field | Old | New | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Variant.custom_fields` / `VariantResponse.custom_fields` | `type: array` | `[array, null]` | Wire delivers `null` on 100% of variants sampled |
| `Variant.config_attributes` / `VariantResponse.config_attributes` | `type: array` | `[array, null]` | Defensive — mirrors `custom_fields` shape |
| `Variant.internal_barcode` / `registered_barcode` (×2 models) | `type: string` | `[string, null]` | Wire delivers `null` on most rows |
| `Inventory.default_storage_bin` | bare `$ref` | `anyOf: [$ref, null]` | Wire delivers `null` on 100% of rows |
| `Inventory.quantity_potential` | `type: string` (required) | `[string, null]` (required) | Key always shipped, value typically `null` |
| `Factory.default_so_delivery_time` / `default_po_lead_time` | `type: string, format: date-time` | `[string, null]` (no format) | Wire delivers `null` or `\"14\"` (days-as-string); Katana's upstream example is wrong |
| `Factory.inventory_closing_date` | `type: string` | `[string, null]` (kept format) | Defensive — sibling fields drift to null |

Where the wire shape is non-obvious (Factory `default_so_delivery_time` / `default_po_lead_time` actually deliver opaque short strings like `"14"` for days, not the documented datetime), the property `description` carries the rationale so it surfaces in the regenerated client docstrings. For the simpler null-tolerance cases (Variant `custom_fields`, `Inventory.default_storage_bin`, etc.) the regression test name does the documenting job — the spec just marks them nullable to match the wire.

Why the wire wins here: Katana's `live-gateway.yaml` ships **zero** response schemas (every 200 is `description: "Return value of ..."` with no `content`). Their README portal ships response examples but no schemas, and the examples are happy-path values that never trigger the null cases. The live API is the only source of truth, and nothing in our existing audit pipeline consults it.

## Why our existing tests missed this

- `validate-response-examples` checks Katana's curated examples against the spec, but their examples don't use `null` for these fields.
- `audit-spec` only compares request DTOs (the live gateway has no response schemas to diff).
- Unit tests construct pydantic objects with `custom_fields=None` (exercising the pydantic side), not `Variant.from_dict({\"custom_fields\": null, ...})` — which is the attrs `from_dict` parser that actually crashed.

New `TestWireNullTolerance` closes this gap by feeding each crash-site shape through the attrs `from_dict` directly. A future regen that re-tightens these to non-nullable will fail those tests.

## Generator + base-class changes

- `scripts/regenerate_client.py` — new regex pattern in `add_ty_type_ignores`: cast `<varname>_data` loop items to `Mapping[str, Any]` before passing to `<Class>.from_dict()`. The openapi-python-client generator now emits union-aware loops where the loop item is inferred as `object` by ty; the existing patcher only handled the literal `data` variable name.
- `katana_public_api_client/models_pydantic/_base.py` — when `_convert_nested_value` encounters an attrs object whose pydantic counterpart isn't in the registry (the case where the spec declares `type: object` inline without a `$ref`, e.g. `FactoryLegalAddress`), fall back to `value.to_dict()`. Previously the attrs object was passed through unchanged and failed pydantic validation downstream.
- `katana_mcp_server/src/katana_mcp/server.py` — persist full per-failure tracebacks in the `cache_warmup_partial` log event. The originating session had `ensure_factory_synced` failing silently for 3 days because the warning carried only `str(exc)`.

## Breaking change — generator class renames

The openapi-python-client generator renames inline `items` classes when the parent property's type union includes `null`:

| Old | New |
| --- | --- |
| `VariantConfigAttributesItem` | `VariantConfigAttributesType0Item` |
| `VariantCustomFieldsItem` | `VariantCustomFieldsType0Item` |
| `VariantResponseConfigAttributesItem` | `VariantResponseConfigAttributesType0Item` |
| `VariantResponseCustomFieldsItem` | `VariantResponseCustomFieldsType0Item` |

These are public symbols (`models/__init__.py` exports them). External importers will fail until they update. Marked as `fix(client)!:` per `COMMIT_STANDARDS.md`.

The only in-tree consumer is `katana_mcp_server/tests/tools/test_items.py`, updated in this PR.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run poe regenerate-client` — generated code reflects new nullable shape
- [x] `uv run poe generate-pydantic` — pydantic mirrors updated
- [x] `uv run poe check` — 3180 unit tests + 19 browser tests pass; ruff/yamllint/ty clean
- [x] Live API verification: `ensure_factory_synced`, `ensure_products_synced`, `ensure_variants_synced` all succeed; `/inventory` parse returns 7 rows for variant FK74003
- [x] Regression: `TestWireNullTolerance` (8 cases) green

It also adds new infrastructure for managing in-memory snapshots and generating local diagnostic reports for sync failures. The most important changes are summarized below.

**Documentation Updates and Feature Slice Transition:**

- Updated references throughout documentation and configuration to point to the new `specs/003-store-activity-data` feature directory, reflecting the transition from validation-only to full activity data storage. Also, new expected file locations for snapshots and diagnostics are documented. **Development Standards and Tooling:**

author: mahiruchan
body:
> Stacks on top of #2 + #3. Merge order: #2 → #3 → this.

Three things, each independently valuable, none touching the others.

## 1. Streaming commit creation (UX fix)

Previously: click \"Stake + create\", page hangs for ~30s, no feedback.

Now: `POST /api/commitments` returns NDJSON, the form renders a live 4-step timeline that fills in as each tx confirms, each step linking to its explorer page:

\`\`\`
✓ createJob   tx → 0x...
✓ setBudget   tx → 0x...
✓ approve     tx → 0x...
⋯ fund        (pending)
\`\`\`

The biggest single UX win in the project.

## 2. x402 coach chat

Per-message accountability coach metered in USDC.

- Schema: \`coach_balance\` (prepaid USDC per session) + \`coach_messages\` (full history)
- `/api/coach/topup` — one real USDC transfer (user → evaluator), credits prepaid
- `/api/coach` — debits \$0.01 per call, runs Kimi-K2.6 against the user's criteria, persists turn
- `CoachChat.tsx` — chat scoped to a commitment, live balance + spend + call count, top-up shortcuts, 402-style \"insufficient balance\" prompt
- System prompt is terse, references the user's criteria, calls out the cost-per-call so the model stays concise

This is the x402 economic model expressed pragmatically: **one real onchain settle per session + internal debits per call**, equivalent to how Circle Gateway batches nanopayments. The HTTP-level x402 dance is already proven in `spike/x402/` and swaps in once Circle publishes a Gateway facilitator on Arc.

## 3. StakeWordVault contract

\`contracts/\` now contains the protocol-owned vault that backs the \"failed stakes fund completers\" narrative.

Surface:

\`\`\`solidity
function recordDeposit(bytes32 commitmentId, address staker, uint256 principal) external onlyKeeper;
function settleCompleted(bytes32 commitmentId) external onlyKeeper;
function settleFailed(bytes32 commitmentId)    external onlyKeeper;
function distributeToWinner(bytes32, address, uint256) external onlyOwner;
function setTeller(IUSYCTeller) external onlyOwner;  // optional, USYC opt-in
function advanceSeason() external onlyOwner;
\`\`\`

Key design choice: **USYC is opt-in**. While the allowlist ticket is pending (24-48h with Circle), \`teller == address(0)\` and the vault books plain USDC. Once allowlisted, owner flips Teller on and subsequent deposits convert automatically. Zero protocol changes either way.

Test suite (\`forge test\`) covers:
- deposit booking + double-record revert
- \`settleCompleted\` refunds the staker
- \`settleFailed\` parks principal for redistribution
- \`distributeToWinner\` pays a completer
- keeper-only / owner-only access control
- season rollover

\`script/Deploy.s.sol\` reads USDC_ADDRESS, KEEPER_ADDRESS, DEPLOYER_PRIVATE_KEY from env.

## Verified

- \`npm run typecheck\` — clean
- \`npm run build --workspace=web\` — production bundle compiles, all 10 routes register
- \`/api/me\` — sessions still auto-provision Circle wallets ✓
- \`/api/coach?commitmentId=x\` (GET) — returns zero balance + empty messages ✓
- \`/api/coach\` (POST, bad id) — 404 with \`{error: \"commitment not found\"}\` ✓
- Forge tests — written and self-contained; not executed locally because GH API rate limit blocked the \`foundryup\` install on this dev box. Any reviewer with forge can run \`cd contracts && forge install foundry-rs/forge-std && forge test\`.

## Misc

- tsconfig target ES2017 → ES2020 (BigInt literals needed for x402 cost math)

## What's next (not in this PR)

- `feat(deploy)`: actually deploy the vault to Arc testnet, wire keeper = evaluator wallet, call \`recordDeposit\` after each fund() and \`settleCompleted\` / \`settleFailed\` from the evaluator service
- `feat(reputation)`: ERC-8004 feedback per settled commitment — the \"Most Novel\" hook
- `feat(ux)`: landing CTA flow + onboarding tour

author: yingchi
body:
## Summary

Implements PER-153 — adds an env-var-gated `skipif` so the two `uv run --no-project --isolated` integration tests can be skipped deterministically on cache-cold / offline hosts.

- `libs/beacon/tests/integration/_offline_guard.py` exposes `_is_offline_or_cache_cold()` (env-var only; no TCP probe to avoid network coupling).
- Both affected test files (`test_append_pending_standalone.py`, `test_record_write_subprocess.py`) gain `pytest.mark.skipif(_is_offline_or_cache_cold(), ...)` via `pytestmark`.
- CI workflow gains a pre-warm step that exercises `uv run --no-project --isolated --with pyyaml python -c "import yaml"` before integration tests run — eliminates first-run flakiness on cache-cold runners.
- `AGENTS.md` documents the env-var workflow.

**Closes PER-153.**

## Design notes

- **Env var, not TCP probe.** A TCP probe to homelab PyPI couples test execution to network behavior, which is precisely what the bot wanted us to avoid in [PR #136 round-6 review](https://github.com/Shadowsong27/agentic-beacon/pull/136). An explicit `BEACON_OFFLINE=1` env var is deterministic and easy to set in CI matrices.
- **Skipif augments `pytest.mark.integration`** — the marker still selects/deselects at suite level; the skipif only fires when the user opts in.

## Delegate correction

The prompt suggested `from libs.beacon.tests.integration._offline_guard import ...`. The delegate noticed `libs/` and `libs/beacon/` lack `__init__.py`, so pytest's package root is `libs/beacon/` — making the correct import `from tests.integration._offline_guard ...`. The delegate flagged this in its structured response. Good catch.

## Test plan

- [x] `BEACON_OFFLINE=1 uv run pytest <target tests> -m integration -q` → `3 skipped` (supervisor re-verified in main env)
- [x] `uv run pytest libs/beacon/tests/integration/ -m integration --collect-only -q` → 78 tests collected, no auto-skip
- [x] `python -c "from tests.integration._offline_guard import _is_offline_or_cache_cold"` → import OK
- [ ] CI green (including the new pre-warm step)
- [ ] opencode-review bot clean

author: mwiebe
body:
### What was the problem/requirement? (What/Why)

The Python implementation of openjd-sessions echos all the `openjd_*:` directives to the log. The Rust implementation does not, but should follow the precedent. It is nice also to have an option to turn the echoing off to clean up the display.

### What was the solution? (How)

Adds SessionConfig::echo_openjd_directives (default true) which controls whether recognised openjd_* directive lines are passed through to log output. When false, directives are still parsed and acted on but filtered from the log. The flag flows consistently from the public API through to ActionFilter without polarity inversion.

body:
See Also: https://github.com/MegaMek/mm-data/pull/356

Previously mental breaks were far too disruptive, far more than was intended. This is due to a disconnect between the behavior ATOW expects and the behavior of the average MHQ player. i.e. ATOW expects the player to spend xp on Willpower to resist the breaks, mhq players don't want to do that (or don't know to do that).

Now campaigns are required to pay a small stipend per week. If paid the mental break will not occur. This cost is `42 * n`, where `n` is the XP cost of the Flaw divided by `100` (rounded normally), with a minimum of `42`.

author: saddlepaddle
body:
## Summary

Apple Git 2.50 (shipped in macOS Sequoia 15.5+ and current Homebrew) refuses to honor an inherited `PAGER` env var on non-interactive callers, erroring with:

\`\`\`
Use of "PAGER" is not permitted without enabling allowUnsafePager
\`\`\`

`simple-git` wraps that stderr as `GitPluginError`, which breaks every git read path used by workspace creation — `git status`, `git worktree list`, `git worktree prune`, `git for-each-ref` — and bubbles up to the renderer as "Couldn't create workspace".

## Fix

One-liner in `getProcessEnvWithShellPath` (`apps/desktop/src/lib/trpc/routers/workspaces/utils/shell-env.ts`), which is the single env builder used by both:

- desktop's simple-git wrapper (`getSimpleGitWithShellPath`)
- the host-service child spawn (`host-service-coordinator.ts:515`)

Setting `GIT_PAGER=cat` cascades to all simple-git calls in desktop main + the host-service's `process.env` → inherited by every `simpleGit()` call inside host-service (13 callsites, mostly without explicit `.env()` overrides).

`GIT_PAGER` takes precedence over `PAGER` for git, so users' interactive terminals still see their preferred pager (delta, less, etc.). Only git inside non-interactive helpers is silenced — pagers are useless in programmatic git invocations anyway.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green
- [ ] On macOS with Apple Git 2.50+ and `PAGER` set in login shell: open Canary → New Workspace → workspace creates without error
- [ ] `~/.superset/host/<org>/host-service.log` no longer shows `GitPluginError: Use of "PAGER" is not permitted...` lines
- [ ] Terminal sessions still respect user's `PAGER` for non-git tools

## Background log evidence (Satya's local Canary)

\`\`\`
[git/getBranchSyncStatus] git.status() failed; treating working tree as clean for this read GitPluginError: Use of "PAGER" is not permitted without enabling allowUnsafePager
[workspace-creation] git worktree list failed: GitPluginError: Use of "PAGER" is not permitted without enabling allowUnsafePager
[workspaceCreation.searchBranches] git for-each-ref failed: GitPluginError: Use of "PAGER" is not permitted without enabling allowUnsafePager
[workspaces.create] worktree prune failed: GitPluginError: Use of "PAGER" is not permitted without enabling allowUnsafePager
\`\`\`

<!-- This is an auto-generated description by cubic. -->
---
## Summary by cubic
Strip `PAGER` and `GIT_PAGER` from the env for all desktop and host-service `git` calls to avoid Apple Git 2.50+ blocking inherited pager vars in non-interactive runs. This restores workspace creation and other git reads while leaving interactive terminals unchanged.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Remove `PAGER` and `GIT_PAGER` in `getProcessEnvWithShellPath`, cascading to all `simple-git` calls and host-service spawns (fixes `git status`, worktree ops, and ref listing).
  - Only set `PATH`/`Path` when `shellPath` is present.

<sup>Written for commit 2570c929d894947717bd726205fbb59d199e5e5e. Summary will update on new commits.</sup>

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a canonical builder to emit CAP 1.2 XML payloads from the message model. 
- Enforce required pre-build rules to prevent invalid CAP messages from being serialized. 
- Ensure CAP-compatible serialization including namespace, UTF-8 bytes, and timezone-aware datetime formatting.

### Description
- Add `builder/xml_builder.py` containing `CAPXMLBuilder` with `build(message: CAPMessage) -> bytes` that returns UTF-8 encoded XML with an XML declaration. 
- Serialize using `lxml.etree` and set the default namespace to `urn:oasis:names:tc:emergency:cap:1.2`. 
- Enforce pre-build validation rules for `sender`, `expires` (at least one `info`), `msgType=Alert` (requires `info`), `scope=Restricted` (requires `restriction`), `scope=Private` (requires `addresses`), and `msgType in {Update, Cancel}` (requires `references`). 
- Support serializing alert and info fields, handle scalar and list values, accept both dict-style and object-style message models, and serialize `datetime` values as ISO-8601 with timezone offset (requires timezone-aware `datetime`). 
- Add configurable pretty-printing via the `pretty_print` constructor flag.

### Testing

body:
### Motivation
- Provide analyzer-scoped TOML configuration for `AnalyzeOptions` so analyzer behavior can be configured from TOML without clashing with controller config and while keeping schema explicit and strict. 

### Description
- New strict TOML parser module at `tailtriage-analyzer/src/options/toml.rs` using private partial structs with `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` to enforce known fields and subgroups under `[analyzer]` only. 
- Added public APIs on `AnalyzeOptions`: `from_toml_str(input: &str) -> Result<Self, AnalyzeConfigError>` and `merge_toml_str(self, input: &str) -> Result<Self, AnalyzeConfigError>`, both validate after applying values and follow the required error rules (missing `[analyzer]`, missing/unsupported `schema_version`, unknown fields/subgroups, type/validation errors).

- **2 new wizard phases:** Personas (Step 2.2, 16 Qs heavy / 4 light) + Domain Modeling (Step 2.7, 11 Qs Full DDD / ~8 DDD-lite / ~6 Light).

body:
## Summary

- **FIX 1 — Language post-filter ported to v3 Tier-2**: YouTube's `relevanceLanguage` is a ranking *hint*, not a hard filter. Korean-titled videos leak into English mandalas (and Latin-only-titled videos leak into Korean mandalas) via the v3 live-search path. The legacy `executor.ts` had a `/[가-힣]/` title guard (~line 978-996) that v3 was missing entirely. This PR ports the filter to both the `runTier2` filter block in `v3/executor.ts` (primary production path) and to `YouTubeProvider.match()` Step 5 in `v3/providers/youtube-provider.ts` (provider abstraction). Adds a `droppedLangMismatch` debug counter alongside the existing `droppedShortsDuration` / `droppedShortsTitle` / `droppedBlocklist` counters. The filter is applied only to Tier-2 live YouTube candidates; Tier-1 `video_pool` matches are already language-filtered at the DB level.

- **FIX 2 — Shorts threshold 60s → 75s; consolidate duplicate constant**: User feedback indicated outputs still surfaced cards slightly over the 60s line; 75s clears that band. Added `export const SHORTS_MAX_DURATION_SEC = 75` to `v2/youtube-client.ts` as the single source of truth. The legacy `executor.ts` previously had a local `const MIN_DURATION_SEC = 60` that was a duplicate; it is now deleted and replaced with an import of `SHORTS_MAX_DURATION_SEC`. Threshold-history doc-comment block in `youtube-client.ts` updated with 2026-05-15 entry. Tests updated: `isShortsByDuration(61)` and `isShortsByDuration(75)` now correctly return `true`; `isShortsByDuration(76)` returns `false`.

## Root causes

- **FIX 1**: `relevanceLanguage=en` is a ranking signal, not a filter contract. YouTube returns Korean-titled results ranked lower but still present. The v3 Tier-2 pipeline had no post-search title check; legacy executor.ts did.

author: jonikanerva
body:
## Why

`SyncEngine.refetchHistory()` did not check the `isSyncing` flag before starting, even though `sync()` does. A `keepDays` change mid-primary-sync therefore fired the backfill task concurrently, letting two writers hit `DataWriter` at the same time and corrupting the `isSyncing` `onChange` edge in `ContentView` (the two operations could each flip the flag to `false` at unrelated points). This violates `docs/swift-code-rules.md` § Core Principles (minimal-scoped fixes for race conditions) and the two-layer architecture's single-writer expectation.

## What

- Add an early-return `guard !isSyncing` to `SyncEngine.refetchHistory()` matching the one already in `sync()`.
- Wrap the flag with `defer { isSyncing = false }` so it cannot leak across error paths (replaces the single manual reset that previously only ran on success/caught-error).
- Document `isSyncing` to make the shared-guard contract between `sync()` and `refetchHistory()` explicit for future maintainers.

## Vision check

Answers against `docs/vision.md` → Non-negotiable product outcomes:

1. Does every ingested article still get a main category assignment? **yes** — fix is purely a sync-orchestration guard; classification path is untouched.
2. Does every ingested article still get a same-story group assignment? **yes** — same as above.
3. Is timeline order still canonical timestamp descending? **yes** — no entry ordering logic touched.
4. Does AI processing leave timeline position unchanged? **yes** — no AI code touched.

## Rules involved

- `docs/swift-code-rules.md` § Core Principles 7 (minimal-scoped changes) — one-line guard fixes the actual race without rippling into call sites.
- `docs/swift-code-rules.md` § Two-layer architecture — restores the single-writer invariant by preventing concurrent backfill + sync against `DataWriter`.

## Verification

- [x] `make test-all` (`$VERIFY_CMD` in `docs/stack.md`) ran green.
- [x] `make lint-fix` is idempotent (no formatting changes produced).
- [ ] Tests added or updated for new logic. — Deferred: `SyncEngine` integration tests land in PR 10, which already plans this coverage. Adding a one-off mock-DataWriter test here duplicates the scaffolding that PR.
- [x] SwiftData `currentSchemaVersion` bumped if the schema changed. — N/A, no schema changes.
- [x] Walked through `docs/definition-of-done.md` — every applicable box checked.

## States handled

N/A — no UI surface added. UI consumers continue to read the single `isSyncing` flag exactly as before.

## Decisions made

Skipped the `SyncState` enum that the architect initially proposed. Devils-advocate input (recorded in agent-teams planning): the underlying problem is one missing guard, not a state-model insufficiency. Introducing an enum would force 5+ call-site updates (`ContentView`, `SettingsView`, `FeederCommands`, `SyncStatusView`, `EntryListView`) with zero observable user benefit, and `docs/swift-code-rules.md` § Core Principles 7 + `docs/autonomy.md` (smallest-surface interpretation) both argue against it. If a future UI surface needs to distinguish primary vs. backfill states, the enum will land in that feature PR.

## Notes for reviewer

`sync()` retains its existing manual `isSyncing = false` resets on both success and error paths — left untouched to keep this PR scoped to the bug. A follow-up could harmonise it with the new `defer` pattern, but that is a refactor, not a fix.

## Summary

The Nova Restaurant CPT (`nova_menu_item`) and its two taxonomies (`nova_menu`, `nova_menu_item_label`) were registered without `show_in_rest => true`. This makes them invisible to consumers that build UI from `GET /wp/v2/types`, including the WordPress.com Calypso dashboard sidebar on Simple sites.

As a result, sites running the Canape (and Confit) theme — which call `add_theme_support( 'nova_menu_item' )` — have a working **Food Menus** menu in classic wp-admin but no equivalent entry in the Calypso sidebar.

This PR adds `show_in_rest => true` to the CPT and both taxonomies, matching the existing pattern in `class-jetpack-portfolio.php` (lines 437, 465, 499) and `class-jetpack-testimonial.php` (line 426).

## Scope is automatic

Nova is gated by `Nova_Restaurant::site_supports_nova()`, which only returns true when:

1. WordPress.com site vertical is `nova_menu`, **or**
2. The active theme calls `add_theme_support( 'nova_menu_item' )`, **or**
3. The `jetpack_enable_cpt` filter returns true for `nova_menu_item`.

Themes that don't opt in get nothing — including the new REST flag. The only themes affected on WordPress.com are **Canape** and **Confit**.

## Fixes

- https://github.com/Automattic/wp-calypso/issues/70753
- Linear: DOTTHEM-133

## Does this pull request change what data or activity we track or use?

No. This PR only changes how an existing post type and its taxonomies are exposed to the WordPress REST API. No new data is collected, stored, or transmitted; no new tracking is introduced.

## Testing instructions

- [ ] On a site with Canape (or Confit) activated and the Custom Content Types Jetpack module enabled, confirm `get_post_type_object( 'nova_menu_item' )->show_in_rest === true`.
- [ ] `GET /wp-json/wp/v2/types/nova_menu_item` returns 200.
- [ ] `GET /wp-json/wp/v2/types` includes `nova_menu_item`.
- [ ] On a sandboxed Simple site, confirm the **Food Menus** entry appears in the Calypso sidebar at `https://wordpress.com/sites/`.
- [ ] Existing wp-admin "Food Menus" submenu (Menu Items / Add Menu Item / Add Many Items / Menu Item Labels / Menu Sections) still works.
- [ ] Editing a menu item still saves the price meta box.
